Modem investigation returned a definitive verdict: **not possible on this unit without the stock TrustZone.**

| Evidence | Finding |
|---|---|
| SMC ABI | `0x82000700` subs 3/4 at 17 sites; encoding `(val<<16)|0` proven by `ubfx #0x11` at `0x17fb8`; WRITE constants `0x8/0x40/0x100/0xA` |
| Runtime | READ → `8`, WRITE `0xA` (CP_PWRON\|CP_START) → `8`; kernel prints `write Fail: 8` |
| MMIO | `CP_CTRL` at PA `0x105C0030` is secure-only (normal-world reads expose only `+0x34/38/40/6C`) |
| TEE | Kinibi t-base-EXYNOS64-V015 with libMcClient/Registry + mcDriverDaemon, but **no modem TA** (`.tlbin`/mcRegistry absent); `libsec-ril` has no TEE path |
| Gates excluded | bootmode/cmdline, sec-boot fuses, sys_rev/ds_det, `CP_RST_N`, SHMEM DT, PMIC (no S2MPU01A) |
| Stock sequence | `MODEM_RESET 0x6f21 → SECURITY_REQ mode2 → XMIT_BOOT → mode0 → MODEM_ON` — already replayed, accepted codes match, still no power |

So the CP’s power switch is guarded by secure firmware that doesn’t authorize a non-Android boot; a Linux-side fix can’t override it. Only the stock Android TZ stack or a bootloader-chain replacement would change that.

All of this is in `docs/reports/modem-tz.md` and the state doc. Remaining live work is device-bound (GPS config reply → NMEA, FM audio/RDS, GPU M1 boot) and still waiting on the **power-cycle + re-plug**.

#!/bin/sh
# Reboot/poweroff for j7elte. busybox reboot(2) does not reset this SoC
# (the kernel's restart handler parks in the bootloader); sysrq 'b' does.
set -eu
sync
echo 1 > /proc/sys/kernel/sysrq
case "${1:-reboot}" in
	poweroff|halt|o) echo o > /proc/sysrq-trigger ;;
	*)               echo b > /proc/sysrq-trigger ;;
esac
EOF

open(p,"w").write(s)
EOF

1. Reduce concurrency: kill some agents, run fewer at a time (e.g., 3-4).
2. Reduce memory pressure: avoid parallel kernel builds (each `make -j2` uses GBs); the integrator builds on external drive; TMPDIR off /tmp.
3. Host /tmp is a 9.7G tmpfs (RAM-backed!) — that's a big OOM contributor. Move build scratch/TMPDIR to disk (/run/media/... external) and clean /tmp artifacts.
4. Disable auto-compaction? Not memory.

# gpu31 IRQ — slot routing, mask/clear completion path, resume re-arm

Date: 2026-11-20. Ticket: `p7580_job_hw_submit` (JS registers written),
IRQ handler (STAT/RAWSTAT clear + fence), IRQ registration/masking,
slot selection. Symptom (Main, int15 silicon): NULL job dispatches on
slot 1 (`run_job seq=0 slot=1 sslot=1 jc=0x2000000`,
`pm_get HELD`, `p7580_job: dispatch slot=1 jc=0x2000000
cfg=0x00083700 as=0 aff=0x3 seq=0`), then no `p7580_job: irq` line,
`panfrost7580-job` IRQ count stays 0 (`panfrost7580-gpu` fired once),
and the fence retires on the 5 s timeout instead of by interrupt.

## 1. Register table (gpu31-jobabi §4/§7 vs what the driver writes)

| Register | Offset | Driver write | Reference | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `JOB_INT_RAWSTAT` | `0x1000` | read in irq-enter + post-start + loop | `[KT]` regmap `:203` raw latch | **added reads** (were missing) |
| `JOB_INT_CLEAR` | `0x1004` | `mask` at init/rearm/recover; per-slot `m` in IRQ | `[KT]` `:204` WO clear; `[V5]` `job_write(JOB_INT_CLEAR, mask)` per slot | match (now also cleared via rearm helper) |
| `JOB_INT_MASK` | `0x1008` | `mask & (js_present \| js_present<<16)` at init/rearm | `[KT]` `:205`; kbase `pm_enable_interrupts` writes `0xFFFFFFFF`; `[V5]` `MK_JS_MASK` union | **kept present-gated** (deliberate: kbase unmasks all 16 slots, this port has 3; unmasked STAT ⊆ RAWSTAT either way) |
| `JOB_INT_STAT` | `0x100C` | read as `status` in IRQ demux | `[KT]` `:206`; `[V5]` handler reads STAT | match |
| `JS_HEAD_NEXT_LO/HI` | `slot+0x40/0x44` | `jc` lo/hi | jobabi §4 `0x1840/0x1844` slot 0 | match |
| `JS_AFFINITY_NEXT_LO/HI` | `slot+0x50/0x54` | full `shader_present` | jobabi §4 | match |
| `JS_CONFIG_NEXT` | `slot+0x58` | `p7580_js_config(as_nr)` = `0x3700\|as` → `0x83700` | jobabi §6: START/END CLEAN_INV + START_MMU(10649) + PRI(8), no FLUSH_REDUCTION/JOBCHAIN/PROTECTED | match (`cfg=0x00083700` trace = `as=0` + `0x83700`) |
| `JS_COMMAND_NEXT` | `slot+0x60` | `START 0x01` after `wmb()` | `[KT]` `JS_COMMAND_START`; `[KB]` GO after cfg | match (**added `wmb()`** — HEAD/AFF/CFG must be visible before START latches on this weakly-ordered SoC) |
| `JS_STATUS` | `slot+0x24` | read in IRQ per-slot + post-start dump | jobabi §7 fault table | match (**added post-start + irq-err naming**) |
| `JS_FLUSH_ID_NEXT` | `slot+0x70` | not programmed | no FLUSH_REDUCTION on T720 | match |
| `JOB_IRQ_THROTTLE` | `0x1014` | untouched (0) | kbase writes throttle cycles per IRQ; 0 = deliver immediately | match (no coalescing) |
| `JOB_IRQ_JS_STATE` | `0x1010` | not read | kbase race-check register (jm_hw.c race comment) | **not ported** (single job per slot here; RAWSTAT tail re-check covers the missed-failure race instead) |

Completion condition (jobabi §4+§7): the dispatched job completes when
the handler observes `JOB_INT_STAT & MK_JS_MASK(slot)` with the DONE
bit set, clears the slot bit(s) via `JOB_INT_CLEAR`, and
`dma_fence_signal()`s the in-flight fence. The 5 s `timedout_job`
exists only for the no-IRQ case. Polarity verified against `[KT]`
regmap `:199-208` + `[V5]` `/tmp/pf52/panfrost_regs.h:191-200`.

INSTR_TYPE_MISMATCH... Hmm.

Think: Midgard fragment job requires the "tiler heap" (JS config bit) and the FBD; but mismatch is instruction type.

Maybe the GPU's JS0 expects fragment jobs to have HEAD pointing to a **job header** whose w0..w3 are command words (fragment job descriptor), and w4 is the header with type. Our dispatch writes JS_HEAD_NEXT = jc and starts. That worked for 60 fragment jobs.

Why would one identical descriptor mismatch? Unless this job's bytes at GPU view differ from CPU view *at execution time* (not at dump time). We dump after fault; by then Mesa may have overwritten the BO (the batch was submitted, then panfrost writes new content). Since we don't fence properly? But excl fence added.

Actually the sequence: panfrost builds batch in a BO, submits, then **reuses the same BO for the next batch** (recycling) while GPU still reading. Our submit returns before GPU completes (async queue!), and Mesa's batch submit waits via syncobj? Panfrost waits on the out fence in its own way... but if our sched queue runs jobs later, Mesa may already reuse.

The excl-fence change was supposed to serialize via resv, but Mesa's own buffer management trusts in-fence/out-fence syncobj: panfrost_batch_submit takes a fence and waits? Not necessarily each frame.

The fault on the LAST submit (frame end) suggests the BO for the frame's fragment job gets reused by the *next* frame's tiler build while GPU still executes → torn.

Our driver's out_sync install happens in run_job (async), so the returned syncobj fence is only populated when the job starts; Mesa may query it earlier and see empty → proceeds to reuse BOs.

Fix: install the fence at SUBMIT (sched_job fence from drm_sched_job_arm is available) rather than in run_job. Earlier int13 showed SUBMIT-time fence was NULL at that point (per probe) — but drm_sched_job_arm should create it. In our shim, job->fence is assigned in pump. Proper fix: create the out fence in the shim at submit time (entity->fence) like mainline drm_sched_job_arm does, and return it via syncobj at SUBMIT. That's the real semantic.

So: shim must create a dma_fence at arm time, assign to sched_job->fence, and run_job's completion signals *that* fence (not a new one).

That's a notable change but correct.

Assign G31_ArmFence: implement arm-time fence in the shim and install it on out_sync at SUBMIT; run_job signals it on completion (via scheduling's finish).

# Panfrost on j7elte — final report (2026-11-21)

## What works (verified on silicon, kernel #37 int25)
- **Render-only DRM node**: `/dev/dri/renderD128` only; no `card0`; Xorg/fbdev untouched.
- **Full v5.2 ioctl surface** through our kernel: GET_PARAM (`0x720`), CREATE_BO (shmem-backed,
  16 MiB OK), MMAP_BO, GET_BO_OFFSET, SUBMIT, WAIT_BO, plus generic DRM syncobj (7 ioctls).
- **Job dispatch and completion**: JS0/JS1 routing per mainline (req0 chain -> JS1, FS -> JS0),
  `JS_CONFIG` per jobabi, IRQ demux (STAT|RAWSTAT), fence signal on IRQ, bounded timeouts,
  PM lifetime + teardown guards, clean close.
- **GPU memory writes**: Zero-fill WRITE_VALUE over a page pre-filled `0xA5A5A5A5` -> both
  kernel (`DEBUG_READ_BO`) and user views read 0. Coherency model (dma_map bind,
  sync_for_device submit, pre-signal sync_for_cpu) verified.
- **Mesa 20.3.5 drives the GPU**: `GL vendor=Panfrost`, `renderer=Mali T720 (Panfrost)`,
  GLES 3.0; hundreds of submits per run; **framebuffer clear is pixel-exact**
  (`RGBA=26,26,102,255`).

## The one open defect
Per frame, exactly one submit faults:
```
p7580_job: ERR slot=0 js_status=0x00000052 (INSTR_TYPE_MISMATCH)
    head=tail=0x21c5600 jc=0x21c5600 seq=121 w4=0x00010013 w5=0 cfg=0x00083700
p7580_job: ERR-MAP ... h6=0x21c5000/0x10000 ... (no overlapping live mappings)
```
- Descriptor bytes are legal (64-bit header, type 9 FRAGMENT), byte-identical in shape to
  fragment jobs that complete.
- Deterministic: same slot, same type, always the last submit of Mesa's flush batch; code
  varies slightly (0x52/0x58) with freed-page contents.
- Fixes tried and verified as *not* the cause: slot routing, JOBCHAIN bit, excl-fence publish,
  IOVA overlap (0 overlaps), arm-time fence install.
- Leading hypothesis after all measurements: the GPU's view of the instruction buffer differs
  from the kernel's view at execution time (BO reuse / PTE-TLB lifetime across Mesa's batch
  pool), i.e. a *visibility/timing* defect, not an encoding one.

## Next experiment (single, decisive)
Instrument the **PTE path at fault time**: on ERR, walk the AS0 page tables for `jc` and compare
the leaf's physical page against the owning BO's current page array, then also re-read that
physical page via `kmap` in the same handler. If they differ, it is a page-table/IOVA lifetime
bug (fix in map/unmap + invalidate ordering); if they match, the GPU's fetch is stale only in
its own cache/TLB and needs a stronger invalidate before `START`.

## Delivered patches (repo)
- `patches/drm-backport/0001-0005` (fence/resv/syncobj/sched shims, 280 host checks)
- `code/gpu31/kms` Mode-B v2 render-only
- `code/gpu31/{gem,jobs,mmu,iommu,power,devfreq,dmabuf}` + driver 0001/0002
- Reports: `gpu31-*.md` (target, iommu, mmu, jobs, gem, dmabuf, kms, drmcore, sched, pm-order,
  close-fix, submit-hw, jobtrace, probernumeric, opsfix, abialign, gpuwrite, coherency,
  mesa-render, tilerchain, primitive, errtrace, instrtype, iova, armfence, integrations 1-25)

## Status summary
| Area | State |
|---|---|
| Kernel driver | complete and stable (render-only, PM, close, syncobj, shmem) |
| GPU execution | works (jobs, IRQ, fences, memory writes) |
| Mesa bring-up | works (renderer, submits, clear) |
| Draw geometry | **open**: one deterministic fragment fault per frame |
| 2D / UI | unaffected, fbdev X healthy |

The walker call is AFTER the dark early-return: if `p7580_drv_pm_get(drv)` returns non-zero (dark), it signals and returns **before** ptewalk. Our PM get apparently returns nonzero in the timeout path → no walk.

Wait: pm_get returns 0 or 1 (success), negative error. Code `if (p7580_drv_pm_get(drv))` treats 1 (already active) as failure! That's a bug: pm_runtime_get_sync returns 1 when already active.

So on timeout, get_sync returns 1 (device active since job holds ref) → treated as "dark" → early return with fence signal, skipping recover AND ptewalk.

That also means **timeout recovery never runs**! And the ERR path is IRQ (separate).

Fix: treat >=0 as success (per earlier comment "may return 1 (already active) or 0... Only negative means dark").

So in timedout_job, the check should be `< 0`. This explains no PTEWALK and no recover.

Also similar misuse may exist elsewhere (pm_get helper already handles: p7580_drv_pm_get returns 0/negative? It returns ret from pm_runtime_get_sync, so 1 possible). Callers using `if (pm_get)` are buggy.

This is a real bug: recover skipped.

Fix: helper should normalize (return 0 on success, negative on error). Check p7580_drv_pm_get implementation: earlier comment said "may return 1 (already active) or 0 (resumed now): both mean powered. Only a negative errno means dark." So callers must check <0. The timedout uses `if (p7580_drv_pm_get(drv))` → wrong.

Patch: change to `< 0`, and audit all call sites.

Assign to a quick fix slice, then rebuild int27 and rerun — this may also fix the fault (recover path) but more importantly enables PTEWALK.

content.text: Found a real bug in the diagnosis path: `pm_runtime_get_sync()` returns **1** when the device is already active, but `p7580_drv_timedout_job()` treats any non-zero as “dark” and **early-returns** — so neither timeout recovery nor the PTEWALK probe ever runs. All `pm_get` call sites need `>= 0` (only negative means dark).

For a fragment job on JS0, the job body starts with the FBD, then shader state commands, then FRAGMENT job command. If the body contains a TILER job command (0x0?) → mismatch.

Given depth and time: it's likely a shader (FS) descriptor issue — Mesa's fragment job jumps to a shader descriptor; if our memory contains unrelocated pointers (shader index), the GPU may read garbage → mismatch.

Fix: use VM_MIXEDMAP + vm_insert_page + get_page/put_page to hold refs.

We pin pages with get_page at create (we do single-ref pin) — but vm_insert_page requires refs too.

Anyway: implement VM_MIXEDMAP fault + refs.

content.text: Root cause of the zeroed shader: the BO’s page is **wiped after Mesa writes it** (a `clear_highpage`-class event during the next BO create/map), because our mmap uses `remap_pfn_range`/`VM_PFNMAP` and holds **no page reference** for the mapping. Rewriting the ISA at every submit removes the fault entirely — so the data, not the code, is being freed underneath.

content.thinking:
Precise cause: tiler consumes PRE-VS content; VS→tiler not visible within one chained submit on this hardware (needs a submit boundary with END clean + in_sync).

Solution: split chain into two submits: VS submit (with END_FLUSH_CLEAN_INV) then TILER submit depending on it. But their experiment (split) faulted JS1 POWER_FAULT — because their split implementation was from the hook (user-space) and duplicated chains incorrectly.

Proper fix in the kernel driver: when a submit's chain contains VERTEX then TILER, split it into two submits (kernel-side), or set END_FLUSH on the vertex job.

Actually Midgard hardware requires a "cache flush" between? kbase submits VS and tiler as separate atoms in a chain? In kbase, each "job" in a chain is separate but the chain includes CACHE_FLUSH job? Kbase's job chain supports only one job per slot; VS and tiler are separate atoms submitted sequentially by userspace (panfrost does 3 ioctls?) Hmm, Mesa submits chain as one ioctl with a list of jobs; the kernel (panfrost 5.2) also submits them as one chain with deps!

But our hardware shows the handoff doesn't work within a chain. Maybe because our chain executes but the VS's writes need "END_FLUSH_CLEAN_INV" on the vertex job itself — panfrost sets JS_CONFIG end-flush per job? Our cfg applies END_FLUSH_CLEAN_INV (bits 12-13) to the *whole* submit, which should flush at end of the chain only.

Per-job cfg isn't a thing (one cfg per submit), so chain-level flush happens at chain end — after tiler already ran. Hence tiler sees stale.

Mainline solution: kbase splits VS and tiler into separate submits? In kbase, atoms are grouped: a "job chain" runs multiple jobs but each job slot is separate; kbase submits vertex/tiler/fragment as separate atoms with dependencies, each with its own JS_CONFIG END flush.

So the correct fix: split the chain into separate submits per job, with dependency, so each gets a flush boundary.

Why did their split fault POWER_FAULT? Because splitting requires the *next* job's header to not be linked (next pointer) and proper deps; their duplicate approach likely re-ran chains.

Implement kernel-side split: in submit, parse the chain (job headers have next pointers) and submit each job as its own sched job with dependency on the previous, sequencing to the same slot? But panfrost UAPI expects one jc per submit; the kernel's drm_sched would run them sequentially on the entity.

Simplest robust approach: driver splits a chained submit into N scheduled sub-jobs (walk next pointers), each with END_FLUSH_CLEAN_INV, deps chained, same slot; the ioctl returns after queueing; completion fence signalled by the last.

That's a significant change but well-defined.

Given the user's persistence, spawn G31_ChainSplit to implement this in the driver, with careful handling (next pointers, jc offsets, refs), build int37, flash, test.

Also Defect B remains (FS ISA zero) — with bins present, FS invoked and faults; needs fixing too. Their REUPLOAD masks it; maybe after split, B still hits.

But B's cause: ISA page intermittently zero despite refs. With mapping refs, why zero? Possibly the BO page is freed by Mesa (GEM close) while a submit still references it? We ref BOs in job->bos (now stamped), so pages held... unless ref taken on wrong object.

Let's focus A (split), then B.

Spawn ChainSplit.

content.text:
Now the mechanism is nailed: within one chained submit the **tiler consumes the pre-VS content** of the position buffer — the VS stores only become visible at the submit’s END flush, which happens after the tiler already ran. Enabling the chain bit doesn’t help.

So the fix is a **submit boundary between VS and tiler** (each with its own flush), done in the driver rather than from userspace.

arguments.context:
# Proven on silicon (int36, docs/reports/gpu31-chainexec.md)
- Mesa submits ONE chain per batch: `WRITE_VALUE(idx2,w4=0x00020005) -> VERTEX(idx1,0x0001000b) -> TILER(idx3,0x0003000f)`, next=NULL terminated; tiler deps on the earlier jobs.
- Control probe: at tiler completion the position buffer already holds the VS triangle, yet **tiles_nonempty=0**.
- Prefill probe: a CPU triangle written into Draw.Position **before** submit is consumed by the tiler (bins exactly tile 0), and the VS provably overwrites it later.
- Conclusion: the tiler reads the PRE-VS content; the VS→tiler handoff is not visible inside one chained submit. Setting JS_CONFIG bit 11 does not change it; JS_CONFIG flushes are per-submit.
- Userspace chain splitting/duplication is not viable (POWER_FAULT, poisoning both slots, watchdog resets).
- Defect B (FS ISA page intermittently all-zero) remains; with bins present the fragment invokes the FS and stalls on 0x52.

Required: kernel-side split of the chain at the VS/TILER boundary (or per job), each submit with END_FLUSH_CLEAN_INV, dependencies chained, same slot semantics, completion fence from the last job; the ioctl must still return a single out_sync covering the whole split.

Files: driver 0001 submit.c (chain walk, sched queueing), code/gpu31/jobs (jm_hw cfg), patches/drm-backport/0004 (deps), docs/reports/gpu31-{chainexec,jobabi,multidep,serialfence}.md.

Repo /tmp/j7repo; patches only; commit own files; external disk only; no flash (Main). Phone on int36; /data tooling; plain runs only (no sync/trace).

tasks.solutionSpace: Kernel-side chain splitting with per-job flush and dependency; must preserve one out_sync and slot semantics.

# Target
Chained submit handling in the driver.

Walk the submitted chain (`next` pointers), enqueue each job as its own scheduled run with END_FLUSH_CLEAN_INV and a dependency on the previous, all on the correct slot; install the ioctl's out_sync on the FINAL job's fence (or a join fence); keep bo list refs and PM lifetime per job. Add host tests for ordering, single out-fence, and error unwinding. Hand to integrator; silicon acceptance = PC2_POLLSCAN control shows the VS triangle's tile set (non-empty, not exactly 1) and pixels advance (red once Defect B is fixed).

# Acceptance
docs/reports/gpu31-chainsplit.md with the design, host tests, and the exact silicon verification. Commit + hand to integrator.

arguments.context:
# Defect B (int36, docs/reports/gpu31-polycensus2.md, gpu31-shaderbo.md, gpu31-mmaprefs.md)
The fragment-shader ISA page (e.g. 0x21d6000, 4 KiB SHMEM BO, GEM handle 8) intermittently reads **all-zero** through `DEBUG_READ_BO` (0xCF) at submit time, even though the ledger shows `count=4 mapcount=1 vma=1 pin=1 up lru swapb clean mapping=0 pgidx=0` with the page reference fix in place. Rewriting the ISA before submit (PAN_FBD_REUPLOAD) removes the fault — so the GPU is reading the page and it is genuinely zero.

Established eliminations: wrong BO/address, never written, tag/meta packing, cache direction, swap/migration, BO close/eviction, VMA mismatch, partial write loss; page refs now held.

Files: code/gpu31/gem (shmem page array, free path, ledger), driver 0001, client 0xCF read; docs/reports/gpu31-{shaderbo,mmaprefs,cachedir,fbdtarget}.md. Phone on int36; /data tooling; plain runs only.

Repo /tmp/j7repo; patches only; commit own files; external disk only; no flash (Main).

content.text:
Defect B is solved analytically and fixed in code: `shmem_getpage_gfp()` leaves a **dirty zero line** in the kernel’s linear alias (this arm64 tree’s `flush_dcache_page()` only clears `PG_dcache_clean`), and because the BO VMA is write-combining, the CPU’s ISA stores go straight to DRAM while that stale line later evicts over them — whole page zeroed 0–5 ms after the write. A 2 s pre-sleep before the write prevents it; 31/32 trials reproduce it without any GPU.

Fix: `__flush_dcache_area(page, PAGE_SIZE)` right after each `shmem_read_mapping_page()`. Building int38 for that.

## SUCCESS 2026-11-22 — hardware 3D renders on j7elte
Kernel **int38** (`42d3a160…`, kernel `3bbcc91a…`) on silicon:

- `pf7580-selftest --defectb-test` → **PASS 32/32**, `lost-immediate=0`, `lost-after-3000us=0`
  (the shmem linear-alias dirty-line defect is fixed by `__flush_dcache_area()`).
- `egltest --offscreen-only` (Mesa 20.3.5, `MESA_LOADER_DRIVER_OVERRIDE=panfrost`) →
  `GL vendor='Panfrost'`, `renderer='Mali T720 (Panfrost)'`, GLES 3.0,
  corner `RGBA=26,26,102,255` (clear), centre `RGBA=255,0,0,255` (triangle),
  **`RENDER_OK` / `PASS`**, three consecutive runs, `ERRCOUNT=0` GPU faults.
- Throughput in that test: 60 draws at 256x256 in ~0.17 s (~350 FPS incl. readback).

Winning fixes that made it work (all in this tree):
1. render-only DRM node (no `card0`), full v5.2 ioctls + syncobj, PM lifetime/teardown guards.
2. job submission: slot routing, IRQ STAT|RAWSTAT demux, arm-time fence + syncobj semantics,
   multi-in-fence dependencies, per-file serialisation.
3. GEM: shmem-backed BOs, `VM_MIXEDMAP` page references, correct cache directions, and the
   `__flush_dcache_area()` fix for the shmem zero-line inheriting over WC stores.
4. driver-side chain split with correct 192-byte VERTEX/TILER payloads, giving the
   VS→tiler submit boundary (flush) that Midgard needs.
5. Mesa 20.3.5 paired with the v5.2 UAPI; attribute-array bounds fix (0007).

Known follow-ups: glmark2 cannot run surfaceless on this stack (canvas only), so benchmark
numbers must come from our own EGL clients; debug probes (`0xCF`, JDBODY/PTEWALK/ledger,
`chain_mode`) are marked for strip before cutover.
EOF
git add docs/reports/gpu31-final.md && git commit -qm "docs: SUCCESS - hardware 3D renders on int38 (RENDER_OK, centre red, 0 errors, 3/3 runs)" && git log --oneline -1

content.text:
Numbers, measured on the phone (same client, same shader, 256×256, readback per frame):

| Engine | Frames | Time | FPS |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Panfrost (Mali T720)** via `egltest` | 60 draws | 0.168 s | **≈357** |
| **llvmpipe (software)** same client | 30 | 0.105 s | **≈472** (and ≈284 at 512²) |

So, honestly: **in this microbenchmark the GPU is not yet faster** — it’s ~25% slower at 256², and at 512² it currently **fails** (52 `TIMEOUT` events; rendering there needs Mesa’s multi-FBD path we don’t support yet).

Why the GPU isn’t winning here:
- The scene is trivial: 3 vertices, 65k pixels — dominated by per-submit overhead (ioctl → sched → chain split → IRQ → fence), not by shading.
- Every frame does a full **readback** (`glReadPixels`), which on our stack costs a sync + cache maintenance; llvmpipe has the pixels in CPU cache already.
- No zero-copy presentation path (panfrost has no KMS/DRM display node; we blit via fb0), so the demo path adds a copy.
- The T720 MP2 at 266–668 MHz is a small GPU; llvmpipe on 8 A53 cores is genuinely competitive for tiny workloads.

Where the GPU should win is fill-heavy, many-frame work — which needs the 512²/MFBD fix and ideally a benchmark that doesn’t read back every frame. That’s the next engineering step if you want a “faster than software” result rather than just correct rendering.

The on-screen demo itself did run purely on the GPU (`GL_RENDERER: Mali T720 (Panfrost)`, 20 fps animated triangle blitted to fb0).

1. **Fault fences are slow, not wrong:** on a fault the ERR path doesn’t signal; the 5 s scheduler timeout does. Fix in flight — kick `timeout_work` at delay 0 from the fault IRQ.
2. **Readback race:** `SUBMIT` returns before the out-fence is published on the BO reservation, so a `WAIT_BO`/`glReadPixels` in that window can read before the job completes. Also confirmed: T720 is **SFBD-only**, so 512² is one FBD; the 4 MiB polygon list is just an 8-px-vs-16-px tile-size over-allocation in Mesa, harmless.

**Fix:** publish only at SUBMIT, inside `serial_lock` (publish order == submit order); no UAPI or recovery change.

Two things from my side for the leak hunt, free to use or ignore:
1. The extra work my patch adds per fragment submit is one `p7580_drv_gpu_read(walk + 40, 4)` — it takes exactly one GEM ref in `p7580_drv_gpu_span()` and drops it on every path in `p7580_drv_gpu_read()`, so it cannot account for pages. `fbd`/`jc_age` are plain u32 fields and the age ledger is a 64-entry array inside `p7580_drv_file` (no allocation). If the leak rate changes at all between int44 and int45 that is worth checking first.
2. In every storm capture the per-frame BO set is *identical*: same 10 handles, same IOVAs, same 64 KiB slab (`h6`) every frame, so the growth is per-page references on reused BOs, not new BOs — consistent with your gem_names finding. Given ~10 BOs/frame and 1.16 MB/frame, the plausible shape is one missing `put_page` per mapped page per submit (mmap pin/unpin or the free-path ref walk), i.e. the same pages get an extra ref each frame while the BOs are reused.

Wall time: 2.06 seconds

The leak is closed and pushed (`44d3c26`).

**int45 silicon**
| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `map == unmap` (iova trace) | **19 : 19** (was 19 : 3) |
| Shmem per 300-frame run | **+24 / +104 / +104 kB** (was ~1.2 MB per frame) |
| ERR / TIMEOUT / WARN | 0 / 0 / 0 across 3 runs |
| Post-exit growth | none (`gem_names` empty) |
| 512² readback | clean, 42–49 fps |

Root cause: `bo_list` held a `drm_gem_object_reference` whose only drop lived in `gem_free_object` — the reference made its own release unreachable, so every submitted BO pinned its private shmem inode, pages and IOVA forever. Fixed by making the entry weak + `kref_get_unless_zero` resurrection only under `bo_lock`, with bind rollback.

Two follow-ups are now in `G31_MMLock`:
1. **Crash**: unlocked `drm_gem_create_mmap_offset`/`free` race `drm_gem_mmap`’s `offset_hash` → `LIST_POISON2` oops in `drm_mm_insert_helper`. Needs a driver-private lock (struct_mutex is unavailable in `free_object`), stress-proven.
2. **fps 101 vs 155**: the formerly-skipped per-frame teardown (288 PTE clears, 3 TLB invalidates, 288 `dma_unmap_page`/`put_page`) needs batching/deferral, measured piece by piece.

Residual open defect, now precisely defined: a **silent `js_status 0x08` timeout, ~1 per 4–6 runs**, costing 750 ms + recovery; worst reproducer is 512² pre-finish readback. int48 (diagnostic overlay: per-class timers behind `prof_arm`, plus independent `submit_err` attribution) is building so a failing run names the error path instead of swallowing it.

arguments.content:
int48 runtime defect, diagnosed from the flashed image: `p7580/prof_arm` does not exist. `p7580_prof_debugfs_init()` calls `debugfs_create_dir("p7580", NULL)`; that directory is already created by the driver, so the call returns `-EEXIST`, `IS_ERR_OR_NULL` is false (it's an ERR_PTR), and the function returns before creating `prof_arm`. My runs printed `can't create /sys/kernel/debug/p7580/prof_arm: Permission denied` and `ls` confirms only chain_mode/dump/ev_arm/hang_inject/iova_arm/job_timeout_ms/serialize_fs/trace_arm.

Fix in the overlay (int49): reuse the existing root dir — `debugfs_lookup("p7580", NULL)` (or keep a drv field for the dir created by the driver) and create `prof_arm` inside it; on `-EEXIST`-class failure log at `p7580perf:` level, never return silently. Also add a probe-time sanity check so this cannot regress unseen.

Separately for the record, from the flashed int48 (unarmed): 4×300 = 158.8 / 105.8 / 155.5 / 151.4 fps, 0 aborts, 0 ERR/TO; 4×512²×40 readback = 60.6 / 54.9 / 38.3 / 39.8 fps, all clean (no timeouts) — so the 0x08 storm did not reproduce in that window.

## GPU stable at 155 fps; leak, race, and fps regression fixed (2026-11-22, int47/int48)
Kernel **int48** (Image 911e7bf1..., boot 70345435...; driver 0001 04db08d, overlay 952ff750...).
- BO/shmem leak: `bo_list` held a strong GEM ref whose only drop lived in `gem_free_object`,
  so every submitted BO pinned its shmem inode for ever (~1.16 MB/frame). Entry is now weak,
  resurrection only via `kref_get_unless_zero` under `bo_lock`; Shmem flat at 2-3 MB across runs.
- mmap-offset race: driver-owned offset manager + one leaf lock; `.mmap` no longer calls
  `drm_gem_mmap`; 1000-iteration churn clean (client bug in the test fixed separately).
- fps 101 -> 155: the 3.10 `dma_fence_wait_timeout` shim returned the bare budget for a
  *signaled* fence, so a 0-jiffy poll looked like "budget exhausted" and `WAIT_BO` (correctly)
  said ETIMEDOUT; Mesa's BO cache never hit (794 WAIT_BO/frame, 4.1 CREATE_BO/frame).
  After the shim fix: 4.3 WAIT_BO/frame, 1.0 CREATE_BO/frame, client sys 5.4 -> 1.7 ms/frame.
- Silicon (locked, uncontended): 300 f at 256^2 = 155.7/155.0/157.4/154.4/158.1 fps, 0 ERR/TO;
  512^2 30-40 f readback clean; 8x512^2x40 readback loop clean.
- Residual: silent `js_status 0x08` timeout ~1 per 4-6 runs (750 ms + recovery). int48's
  diagnostic overlay should name it, but `p7580/prof_arm` fails to register
  (`debugfs_create_dir("p7580")` returns -EEXIST); int49 fixes that. `submit_err` now logs
  `n=` and is independent of the 8-line sched_trace budget.
'''
open(p,'w').write(s.rstrip()+'\n'+add)

Vendor DRM/display stack in the kernel tree above.

# Questions
1. `drm_atomic_support`: does `drivers/gpu/drm/exynos/` implement atomic modesetting (`drm_atomic_helper_*`, `atomic_commit`, `drm_crtc_funcs.atomic_*`, `drm_plane` + universal planes)? Kernel version of the DRM core it is written against. If absent, name exactly what is missing (e.g. `atomic_check/commit`, `drm_atomic_state`, plane update path).
2. `decon_binding`: how `decon_fb` (14830000.decon_fb) binds and owns CRTC/planes/windows; which driver creates `/dev/fb0`; is there any in-tree DRM KMS implementation of these windows (grep for crtc/plane in decon_7580), or only an fb API? Can the fb driver be made to register a DRM CRTC instead, and where would that hook go?
3. `dt_nodes`: DT compatibles for decon/decon_fb/DSI on this SoC (`14830000.decon_fb`, `decon_tv`, dsi), which ones `exynos_drm` matches, and whether the DTS marks them `status = "okay"`.
4. `kconfig_state`: the exact `CONFIG_DRM_EXYNOS*`/`CONFIG_FB_DECON*`/`CONFIG_DRM_PANFROST7580` symbols, their values in the built .config if present, and which Makefiles/Kconfigs gate the decon fb vs DRM paths.
5. `crtc_plane_api`: in `decon_7580`/`decon_display`, the functions that program windows (WINCON, shadow registers), commit/trigger, and vblank/teardown; whether there is a `decon_update_plane`-style API already.
6. `conflicts`: what prevents binding `exynos_drm` today (driver-ownership clash with `decon_fb`, missing DT phandles, missing clocks/regulators/power domains, DRIVER_RENDER_ONLY-style gating), with evidence.
7. `reuse_options`: rank the three options — (a) extend vendor `exynos_drm` with atomic and a DECON CRTC backed by the existing window API, (b) port modern mainline `exynos_drm`/`decon5` KMS into 3.10, (c) a new minimal KMS driver exposing one CRTC + one primary plane for this display — by the evidence you found (amount of missing code, API mismatch, risk).

# Acceptance
All seven answered with file:line citations; no edits to the kernel tree; report only.

ABSENT — neither the vendor exynos DRM driver nor the 3.10 DRM core in this tree has atomic modesetting.

Driver side: `grep -E 'drm_atomic|atomic_commit|atomic_check|atomic_update|drm_plane_helper|DRIVER_ATOMIC|drm_universal_plane' drivers/gpu/drm/exynos/*.c` → 0 matches (only `atomic_t` fields in exynos_drm_crtc.c:52/236/357). CRTC and plane vtable entries are purely legacy:
- `static struct drm_crtc_funcs exynos_crtc_funcs = { .set_config = drm_crtc_helper_set_config, .page_flip, .destroy, .set_property }` — drivers/gpu/drm/exynos/exynos_drm_crtc.c:307-311
- `static struct drm_crtc_helper_funcs exynos_crtc_helper_funcs = { .dpms, .prepare, .commit, .mode_fixup, .mode_set, .mode_set_base, .load_lut, .disable }` — exynos_drm_crtc.c:188-197

Core side (this is a pre-atomic DRM, Samsung's 3.10.108 fork):
- No `include/drm/drm_atomic.h`, no `drm_atomic_helper.h`, no `drm_plane_helper.h`, no `drm_mipi_dsi.h` (full listing of include/drm/ shows only drmP.h, drm_crtc.h, drm_crtc_helper.h, drm_fb_helper.h, drm_dp_helper.h, drm_edid.h, drm_fb_cma_helper.h, drm_gem_cma_helper.h, drm_encoder_slave.h …).

- `int drm_plane_init(...)` is still implemented inside drivers/gpu/drm/drm_crtc.c:806 (planes were not split into drm_plane.c until later).
- `include/drm/drm_crtc.h:331` `struct drm_crtc_funcs` has only save/restore/set_config/cursor/page_flip/destroy/set_property; `:633` `struct drm_plane_funcs` = update_plane/disable_plane/destroy/set_property; `:890` `drm_plane_init(..., bool priv)` — no `drm_universal_plane_init`, no `struct drm_crtc_state/plane_state/connector_state`, no `atomic_begin/flush`, no atomic property blobs.

Core vintage: DRM_MAJOR 226 at include/drm/drmP.h:306; drmP.h + drm_crtc_helper/drm_fb_helper design = Linux 3.10/3.11-era DRM (atomic landed upstream after this fork).
data.decon_binding:
`decon_fb@14830000` is bound by the vendor fbdev platform driver, not by DRM.

Binding: `static const struct of_device_id decon_device_table[] = { { .compatible = "samsung,exynos5-decon_driver" } }` — drivers/video/exynos/decon_7580/decon_core.c:55-58; `static struct platform_driver decon_driver __refdata = { .probe = decon_probe, .remove = decon_remove, .shutdown = decon_shutdown, … }` — decon_core.c:4867-4874, registered from `late_initcall(exynos_decon_register)` at decon_core.c:4880-4890.

Probe (`decon_probe`, decon_core.c:4385) in order: clocks via `decon_int_get_clocks()` (decon-int_drv.c:130; requires pclk_decon0, aclk_decon0, decon0_eclk, decon0_vclk, aclk_disp, mif_pll, aclk_disp_200 — decon-int_drv.c:132-186); `devm_request_and_ioremap` of reg[0] (decon_core.c:4430-4431); IRQs (3 of them) via `decon_int_register_irq` (decon-int_drv.c:765); vsync/psr kthreads; TE eint (`decon_fb_config_eint_for_te`, decon-int_drv.c:808); debugfs; `ion_client_create` (decon_core.c:4470); v4l2/media entity registration (`decon_register_entity`, decon_core.c:4532); `iovmm_activate` (decon_core.c:4559); window acquisition (`decon_acquire_window`, decon_core.c:4564 → :2919); media-device lookup `module_name_to_driver_data(MDEV_MODULE_NAME)` (decon_core.c:4571, fails probe if absent); link/subdev creation; then `register_framebuffer(decon->windows[decon->pdata->default_win]->fbinfo)` (decon_core.c:4590-4591).

CRTC/plane ownership is expressed as fb_info-per-window, not DRM objects:
- `struct decon_win { struct decon_fb_pd_win windata; struct decon_device *decon; struct fb_info *fbinfo; struct media_pad pad; struct decon_fb_videomode win_mode; struct decon_dma_buf_data dma_buf_data[MAX_BUF_PLANE_CNT]; … }` — decon.h:223-232
- `struct decon_device { … struct decon_win *windows[MAX_DECON_WIN]; … }` — decon.h:644-650
- `decon_acquire_windows()` allocates one `framebuffer_alloc()` per window, assigns `.fbops = &decon_fb_ops`, allocates cmap (decon_core.c:2836-2914; fb_ops at decon_core.c:2499-2515). Only the default window (win 0, dtsi default_win=<0>, exynos7580.dtsi:1213-1214) actually backs a display buffer via `decon_fb_alloc_memory` (decon_core.c:2877-2884, :2739) and is the one registered → this creates **/dev/fb0**.
- Plane-style updates come from an fb-private ioctl: `#define S3CFB_WIN_CONFIG _IOW('F', 209, struct decon_win_config_data)` (decon.h:889-890), handled by `decon_ioctl` (decon_core.c:2372) → `decon_set_win_config` (decon_core.c:2185). Windows 1..max_win-1 have fb_info but are never registered as fb devices.

No DRM KMS implementation of these windows exists in the tree: `grep -E 'drm_|crtc|plane' drivers/video/exynos/decon_7580/*.c` returns only a local variable named `crtc` in the FBIO_WAITFORVSYNC ioctl (decon_core.c:2379,2388-2396). Same for the other decon trees (`drivers/video/exynos/decon/`, `decon_display/`, `decon_tv_display/`): only a `struct vpp_drm_log` name (drivers/video/exynos/decon/decon.h:619). There is no exynos DRM DSI host either (`drivers/gpu/drm/exynos/exynos_drm_dsi.c` does not exist).

Can the fb driver register a DRM CRTC instead, and where? Structurally yes, and the hook points are concrete:
(1) Adapter object: the vendor DRM core already defines the exact callback sets a DECON CRTC would implement — `struct exynos_drm_manager_ops { dpms, apply, mode_fixup, mode_set, get_max_resol, commit, enable_vblank, disable_vblank, wait_for_vblank }` (exynos_drm_drv.h:173-187) and `struct exynos_drm_overlay_ops { mode_set, commit, enable, disable }` (exynos_drm_drv.h:64-70), paired with `exynos_drm_subdrv_register()` (drv.h:313, exynos_drm_core.c:186-196).
(2) Registration call site: in `decon_probe` right after `decon_acquire_window()` (decon_core.c:4564) and either instead of / next to `register_framebuffer()` (decon_core.c:4588-4596) — call `exynos_drm_subdrv_register()` with a manager whose ops translate to `decon_enable`/`decon_disable`/`decon_set_win_config`.
(3) Commit/flip: `decon_pan_display` (decon-int_drv.c:542-615) is already an exact page-flip implementation (shadow protect → `decon_reg_set_regs_data` → VIDW_ADD0 write → unprotect → `decon_reg_activate_window` → trigger → `decon_wait_for_vsync`); `decon_update_regs` (decon_core.c:2066-2160) is the fence-aware commit worker.
(4) vblank: `decon_wait_for_vsync` (decon_core.c:1226) plus `decon->vsync_info.timestamp/wake` in the IRQ handler (decon-int_drv.c:97-98) and the vsync kthread (decon-int_drv.c:871-882) map directly onto `enable_vblank/disable_vblank`.
Blocker for a *separate* module: the decon module exports only `decon_int_drvdata` (decon_core.c:65-66) plus the fb entry points `decon_set_par/decon_setcolreg/decon_pan_display/decon_mmap` (EXPORT_SYMBOL at decon-int_drv.c:386, 534, 615, 636). `decon_set_win_config`, `decon_update_regs`, `decon_enable`, `decon_disable`, `decon_reg_*` are non-exported, so a CRTC glued on from *another* module requires either new EXPORT_SYMBOLs or (cleaner) the CRTC living inside `drivers/video/exynos/decon_7580/`.

Nodes (SoC file arch/arm64/boot/dts/exynos7580.dtsi):
- `decon_0: decon_fb@14830000 { compatible = "samsung,exynos5-decon_driver"; reg = <0x0 0x14830000 0x0 0x8000>; samsung,power-domain = <&pd_disp>; interrupts = <0 203 0>, <0 201 0>, <0 202 0>; ip_ver = <4>; max_win = <3>; n_sink_pad = <3>; n_src_pad = <1>; default_win = <0>; trig_mode = <0>; dsi_mode = <0>; status = "disabled"; }` — exynos7580.dtsi:1078-1152 (compatible :1079, power domain :1082, irqs :1085, 20+ clocks/clock-names :1088-1211, max_win :1214, default_win :1218, status disabled :1152)

- `mdev_0: mdev_output { compatible = "samsung,exynos5-mdev"; }` — exynos7580.dtsi:1165-1167 (required by decon probe)
- `pd_disp: pd-disp@10464080 { compatible = "samsung,exynos-pd"; … }` — exynos7580.dtsi:1654-1659
- There is NO `decon_tv` node in exynos7580.dtsi (grep `decon_tv` → no match); the TV driver's compatible `"samsung,exynos5-decon_tv_driver"` exists only in drivers/video/exynos/decon_tv_display/decon_tv_drv.c:37-40, and CONFIG_EXYNOS_DECON_TV_DISPLAY is not set.

Board-level enablement (both nodes are disabled at SoC level and switched on per board, e.g. j7elte): `decon_fb@14830000 { gpios = <&gpd0 7 0xf>; psr_mode = <0>; trig_mode = <1>; disp-pll-clk = <64500000>; gpio_err = <&gpa3 7 0x1>; status = "okay"; }` and `dsim_0 { lcd_info = <&ea8061>; decon_board = <&decon_board_list>; status = "okay"; }` — arch/arm64/boot/dts/exynos7580-j7elte_rev06.dts:1009-1026; panel power sequencing (`LCD_1P8`, `LCD_3P0`, reset GPIO gpd1-3) at :1027-1042. Boards for other products do the same (e.g. exynos7580-a3xelte_eur_open_00.dts:1237-1253).

What `exynos_drm` matches: nothing in this DT. The DRM "master" driver has NO of_device_id — `static struct platform_driver exynos_drm_platform_driver = { .probe = …, .driver = { .name = "exynos-drm" } }` (drivers/gpu/drm/exynos/exynos_drm_drv.c:312-320), and the device is created in-code with `platform_device_register_simple("exynos-drm", -1, NULL, 0)` (exynos_drm_drv.c:393). Encoders/connectors come only from registered *subdrivers*; their DT tables are:

- hdmi: `"samsung,exynos5-hdmi"` — exynos_hdmi.c:1928-1934; mixer: `"samsung,exynos5-mixer"` — exynos_mixer.c:1153-1159; ddc: `"samsung,exynos5-hdmiddc"` — exynos_ddc.c:52-57; hdmiphy: `"samsung,exynos5-hdmiphy"` — exynos_hdmiphy.c:50-56

data.crtc_plane_api:
There IS a complete plane/window programming API — it is just fb-shaped, and it already contains a `decon_update_plane` analogue.

Per-frame window config (plane update): `decon_set_win_config(struct decon_device *, struct decon_win_config_data *)` — decon_core.c:2185-2365. It walks `win_config[i]` (states DECON_WIN_STATE_DISABLED/COLOR/BUFFER, decon.h:356-...) and for buffers calls `decon_set_win_buffer()` (decon_core.c:1516-1737: format→fb var, plane count, ion handle / dma_buf attach, `dma_buf_data[]` fill) then builds `struct decon_reg_data` (`wincon[]`, `winmap[]`, `vidosd_a/b[]`, `dma_buf_data[][]`, `num_of_window`, `bandwidth`) and enqueues it on `update_regs_list` + `queue_kthread_work(&decon->update_regs_worker, …)` (decon_core.c:2346-2358).

Commit/trigger: `decon_update_regs()` — decon_core.c:2066-2160 — waits fences, runs `__decon_update_regs()`, then `decon_wait_for_vsync(decon, VSYNC_TIMEOUT_MSEC)`, `decon_reg_wait_for_update_timeout(DECON_INT, 300*1000)` (shadow-update completion), re-arms/disarms the HW trigger and `sw_sync_timeline_inc()` — driven by `decon_update_regs_handler()` kthread work (decon_core.c:2162-2183).

Register level (drivers/video/exynos/decon_7580/decon_reg_7580.c):
- `decon_reg_set_regs_data()` :529-567 — writes `WINCON(win_idx)` (:543) with the burstlen fixup, `WIN_MAP(win_idx)` (:544), channel map via `WINCHMAP0` (:546), then VIDOSD/VIDW address registers.
- WINCON/shadow handling: `decon_reg_shadow_protect_win()` :640-645 (SHADOWCON win protect), `decon_reg_activate_window()` :648-652 (`WINCON_ENWIN` + `decon_reg_update_standalone`), `decon_reg_clear_win()` :94-101, `decon_reg_set_block_mode()` :654-668, `decon_reg_update_standalone()` :179-182, `decon_reg_wait_for_update_timeout()` :616-638, `decon_reg_is_win_enabled()` :297-303.
- Trigger: `decon_reg_set_trigger()` :599-613 (TRIGCON, tracks `decon->trigger_enable`), `decon_reg_configure_trigger()` :201-216, `decon_reg_set_int()` :569-595; `decon_reg_start()` :480-490 / `decon_reg_stop()` :492-527; mode programming `decon_reg_init()` :414-446, `decon_reg_init_probe()` :447-478, `decon_reg_configure_lcd()` :184-200, `decon_reg_set_porch()` :131-150, `decon_reg_set_vidout()` :54-66, `decon_reg_set_default_win_channel()` :38-43.

Flip path (closest to `drm_crtc_funcs.page_flip`): `decon_pan_display()` — decon-int_drv.c:542-615 — computes byte offsets, `decon_reg_shadow_protect_win(…,1)`, `decon_reg_set_regs_data()`, `writel(fix.smem_start+start_boff, regs+VIDW_ADD0(idx))`, unprotect, `decon_reg_activate_window()`, `decon_activate_window_dma()`, HW-trigger enable, then `decon_wait_for_vsync()`.

Enable/disable (CRTC dpms/mode_set equivalent): `decon_enable()` decon_core.c:894-1011 (pm_runtime_get_sync, iovmm_activate, DSIM `s_stream(1)` via v4l2_subdev_call, `decon_reg_init(DECON_INT, dsi_mode, &p)`, `decon_reg_start`, IRQ unmask) and `decon_disable()` decon_core.c:1014-1127.

Vblank/IRQ: `decon_int_irq_handler()` — decon-int_drv.c:73-124 — handles VIDINTCON1_INT_FRAME / INT_FIFO / INT_I80, sets `decon->vsync_info.timestamp` and `wake_up_interruptible_all(&decon->vsync_info.wait)` (:97-98). `decon_wait_for_vsync()` decon_core.c:1226-1266; a dedicated vsync kthread `decon_int_create_vsync_thread()` decon-int_drv.c:871-889 (wait loop :839-842) exposes `…/vsync`; FBIO_WAITFORVSYNC via decon_ioctl (decon_core.c:2387-2396). TE/eint in MIPI-command mode: `decon_fb_isr_for_eint()` decon-int_drv.c:717-763 (SW-trigger re-arm + DSIM PKT_GO) — note the j7elte board sets `trig_mode = <1>` (SW trigger), j7elte_rev06.dts:1012.

Teardown: `decon_remove()` decon_core.c:4819-4840 — pm_runtime_disable, decon_put_clocks, iovmm_deactivate, `unregister_framebuffer(decon->windows[0]->fbinfo)` (:4829), kthread_stop(update_regs_thread), `decon_release_windows()` per window, debugfs_remove_recursive; `decon_shutdown()` :4844. There is no DRM object to destroy because none is created.
data.conflicts:
What prevents `exynos_drm` from producing card0 today, strongest first:

1. **No subdriver → -EINVAL by construction.** `exynos_drm_load()` calls `exynos_drm_device_register(dev)` (exynos_drm_drv.c:107-109); that function counts registered subdrivers and `if (!fine_cnt) return -EINVAL;` (exynos_drm_core.c:132-136). Since no exynos subdriver matches `samsung,exynos5-decon_driver` (see dt_nodes), fine_cnt==0 always, load() unwinds (`goto err_vblank` → drm_release_iommu_mapping/mode_config_cleanup), `drm_platform_init()` fails, probe fails, and no `card0`/`controlD64` is created. `MAX_CRTC 3` / `MAX_PLANE 5` (exynos_drm_drv.h:20-21) CRTCs are created up-front (drv.c:81-99) but are orphaned shells with no manager ops. Hardware observation matches: "/sys/class/drm holds only `version` … no driver bound (vendor 3.10 has no exynos-DRM match for this SoC)" — /tmp/j7repo/docs/SESSION-STATE.md:283-289 and :300-306.

2. **Driver-ownership clash on 14830000.** The node is a single-owner platform device: the fbdev `decon_driver` claims it via compatible (decon_core.c:55-58, 4867-4874, late_initcall :4880-4890) and ioremaps reg[0], takes 3 IRQs, clocks, the pd_disp domain and registers /dev/fb0 (decon_core.c:4430-4431, 4591). Any DRM driver that wants the same registers must either (a) reuse that compatible (of_match cannot bind two drivers), (b) invent a new compatible → requires editing the shipped DTS/DTB, which is a brick risk per the project's S-Boot payload rule (/tmp/j7repo/patches/drm-kms-coexist/DESIGN.md §1.2, §4), or (c) run inside the decon driver (see reuse_options a). A prior attempt (patches/drm, 'samsung,exynos7580-decon-drm') did exactly (b) and had to disable EXYNOS_DECON_EXYNOS7580/EXYNOS_MIPI_DSI/panel — i.e. it stole fb0, killing the Xorg fbdev fallback (DESIGN.md §1.2).

3. **Probe prerequisites beyond regs/irqs** (all must be satisfied by whoever owns the pipe; each is a probe failure if missing): pd_disp power domain (dtsi:1082, 1654-1659); the 20-entry clock list incl. pclk_decon0/aclk_decon0/decon0_eclk/decon0_vclk/aclk_disp/mif_pll (dtsi:1088-1211 vs decon-int_drv.c:132-186); the v4l2 media device `samsung,exynos5-mdev` (dtsi:1165-1167 → decon_core.c:4571-4575, hard `goto fail_iovmm`); ION (`ion_client_create`, decon_core.c:4470); exynos iovmm (iovmm_activate, decon_core.c:4559); DSIM subdev + `lcd_info` hostdata (used by decon_enable via `v4l2_subdev_call(... s_stream)`, decon_core.c:938-945) and the panel/regulator list `decon_board_list` (j7elte_rev06.dts:1027-1042).

4. **fbdev-emulation collision when KMS later exists.** Both stacks call `register_framebuffer()` for the first fb (decon_core.c:4591; DRM side would go through drm_fb_helper, exynos_drm_fbdev.c:65-76,139+). The second registration fails with -EBUSY because the fb index is global — so keeping fb0 from decon while also doing DRM fbdev emulation is not possible; DRM must either own the display or run without fbdev emulation (kwin can use the DRM node directly).

5. **Render-node gating is local, not upstream** (so no barrier, but a bookkeeping fact): `DRIVER_RENDER_ONLY 0x8000` is added by /tmp/j7repo/code/gpu31/kms/0001-drm-3.10-render-node-mode-b.patch (line 307 of that patch) because stock drmP.h stops at `DRIVER_PRIME 0x4000` (include/drm/drmP.h:150-158). panfrost7580 sets `.driver_features = DRIVER_GEM | DRIVER_PRIME | DRIVER_RENDER_ONLY` (code/gpu31/driver/0001-…patch:5835-5836) and deliberately has no DRIVER_MODESET/card0 (same patch :5566-5570, :7777-7780) because Xorg auto-probed card0 and hung (docs/SESSION-STATE.md:283-290). It binds `mali@0x11400000`, a different platform device — so it does not conflict with a future DECON KMS driver; the two can coexist as two DRM devices (renderD128 + card0).
data.reuse_options:
Ranked by evidence (missing code, API mismatch, risk). Score: (a) is the only option whose hardware half already exists.

(a) Extend vendor exynos_drm with atomic + a DECON CRTC backed by the existing window API — RECOMMENDED, but note an important split: the window/mode/vblank machinery is *already written and shipping* (decon_set_win_config :2185, decon_set_win_buffer :1516, decon_update_regs :2066, decon_pan_display int_drv:542, decon_enable/disable :894/:1014, decon_reg_* reg_7580.c:414-668, IRQ/vsync int_drv:73-124/871-889). What is missing is (i) the atomic core itself (drm_atomic_state + helpers + DRM_IOCTL_MODE_ATOMIC + universal planes + DRIVER_ATOMIC — a ~2–3kLoC backport of upstream 3.14–3.15 drm_atomic.c/drm_atomic_helper.c/drm_plane_helper.c onto a 3.10 drm_crtc_helper core), and (ii) a CRTC/plane adapter: manager_ops (drv.h:173-187) + overlay_ops (drv.h:64-70) → decon calls, plus exports (only decon_int_drvdata is exported, decon_core.c:65-66). Risk: medium-high on the DRM-core side (atomic helpers assume drm_plane.c, drm_framebuffer.c, drm_atomic_state, blob properties, and changed page-flip/fbdev helper APIs that this fork predates), low-medium on the hardware side. Precedent in-repo: the panfrost series already proved they will patch the 3.10 DRM core for a new feature (DRIVER_RENDER_ONLY patch, code/gpu31/kms/0001-…patch), so a core backport is an accepted technique here, and the fbdev driver stays intact as fallback as long as the DECON CRTC lives *inside* decon_7580 (no DT change, no compatible theft).

(b) Port modern mainline exynos_drm/decon5 KMS into 3.10 — NOT recommended. Concrete mismatches: mainline decon5 needs `drm_atomic_helper`, `drm_crtc_state/plane_state`, `drm_universal_plane_init`, `drm_bridge`, `drm_mipi_dsi` host framework, `drm_fbdev_generic`, `drm_gem_dma_helper`, plus CCF/`drm_display_mode`/`of_graph` plumbing — none exist here (no include/drm/drm_atomic.h, drm_mipi_dsi.h, drm_bridge.h; drm-y list at drivers/gpu/drm/Makefile:7-15; drm_plane_init still in drm_crtc.c:806). The DECON register programming in mainline also targets a different IP generation (decon5/7 with different WINCON/VIDOSD layout and DPU/CMD mode), so the existing 7580 register file (decon_reg_7580.c, regs-decon.h) would have to be re-derived. Evidence of that gap inside the repo: the earlier `exynos7580_drm` attempt had to re-implement panel/DSIM programming from scratch and could not keep fb0 (DESIGN.md §1.1–§1.2, §4).

(c) A new minimal KMS driver exposing one CRTC + one primary plane — VIABLE FALLBACK, medium risk, small code but duplicates hardware knowledge. The minimum for kwin_wayland 6.8 is atomic + universal planes, so a 'minimal' driver still needs the atomic core backport from (a); with atomic present, the driver itself is small: one CRTC (prepare/enable/disable/mode_set → decon_reg_init/decon_reg_start/decon_reg_stop, reg_7580.c:414/480/492), one primary plane (atomic_update → config struct + decon_set_win_config :2185), one connector + DSI panel mode from `lcd_info`/ea8061, vblank from the FRAME/I80 IRQ (int_drv:73-124) and page_flip from `decon_pan_display` logic. arguments.content:
# DECON KMS + atomic plan (Plasma Mobile prerequisite)

Status: **scoped, not started**. Owner: this repo. Evidence: `DeconKmsSurvey`
(survey of the vendor tree, all citations below are file:line in
`android_kernel_samsung_universal7580/`).

## 1. What blocks Plasma Mobile today

| Fact | Evidence |
|---|---|
| Plasma Mobile 6.8.3 + kwin 6.8.3 are already installed on the phone | `apk list -I`; `startplasmamobile`, `kwin_wayland` present |
| No KMS node: only `renderD128` | `/sys/class/drm/` on device |
| Display owned by legacy fbdev `decon_fb` | `decon_core.c:55-58, 4867-4890`; `/sys/bus/platform/drivers/decon/14830000.decon_fb` |
| `exynos-drm` has **no** device bound and cannot bind | `exynos_drm_core.c:132-136` returns `-EINVAL` with `fine_cnt == 0`; no exynos subdriver matches `samsung,exynos5-decon_driver` |
| The 3.10 DRM core has **no atomic at all** | no `drm_atomic.h`, no `DRIVER_ATOMIC` (`drmP.h:144-158`), `drm_plane_init` still in `drm_crtc.c:806`, `drm-y` has no `drm_atomic.o`/`drm_plane.o` |
| The vendor CRTC/plane vtables are legacy-only | `exynos_drm_crtc.c:188-197, 307-311`; `exynos_drm_plane.c:246-251` |
| KWin 6 requires atomic + universal planes | upstream requirement; reason M3 below matters |

So the missing piece is not a config switch: it is a **DRM atomic core backport plus a
DECON KMS subdriver**. The good news is that the hardware half already exists and ships
in the fbdev driver: window programming (`decon_set_win_config`, `decon_core.c:2185-2365`),
buffer/dma-buf attach (`decon_set_win_buffer`, `:1516-1737`), commit + shadow registers
(`decon_update_regs`, `:2066-2183`), enable/disable (`:894-1127`), vsync
(`decon-int_drv.c:73-124, 542-615`), and register programming (`decon_reg_7580.c:414-668`).

## 2. Chosen approach (ranked in the survey)

**(a) Extend the vendor `exynos_drm` with an atomic core + a DECON CRTC** backed by the
existing window API. Chosen because it reuses ~all hardware code; the alternative
(b) porting mainline `exynos_drm`/`decon5` drags in newer clock/power/DSI APIs that do not
exist in 3.10, and (c) a from-scratch minimal KMS still needs the same atomic core.

Hard constraint learned from the earlier attempt (`patches/drm-kms-coexist/DESIGN.md`):
**do not steal the `samsung,exynos5-decon_driver` / `samsung,exynos5-mipi-dsi`
compatibles** — that attempt bound DRM to them, the fbdev driver lost its device, and the
screen went dark with no `fb0`. Coexistence must be explicit (see M3).

## 3. Milestones

**M0 — atomic core backport (build-only; no device risk)**
Backport from Linux 3.14/3.15 into this 3.10 DRM core: `drm_atomic.c`,
`drm_atomic_helper.c`, `drm_plane.c`, `drm_framebuffer.c` (split out of `drm_crtc.c`),
plane helper, universal planes, `DRIVER_ATOMIC`, `DRM_IOCTL_MODE_ATOMIC`,
`DRM_CLIENT_CAP_ATOMIC`, atomic state structs + properties (`include/drm/drm_atomic.h`,
`drm_atomic_helper.h`, `drm_plane_helper.h`), plus `drm_modeset_lock`/crtc-state plumbing.
Constraint: must not regress the existing legacy paths other drivers use (this tree still
builds `exynos_drm` legacy + fbdev).
Acceptance: kernel builds clean; no new warnings in touched files; host-side compile of
the DRM core; boot on the phone with the same fb0/UI (atomic core present but unused);
`DRM_CLIENT_CAP_ATOMIC` reachable.
Estimate: 1–2 focused days.

**M1 — DECON KMS subdriver (card0, no compositor yet)**
New `exynos_drm_decon.c` subdriver: one CRTC + one primary plane + one overlay, encoder +
DSI connector (`dsim_0`), atomic check/commit implemented over
`decon_set_win_config`/`decon_update_regs`, vblank from the existing vsync work,
`drm_fb_helper` fbdev emulation on KMS. Modes from the panel (`ea8061`) timings already in
the board DTS. Coexistence: bind only when the legacy fb driver is disabled/absent, or via
an explicit Kconfig choice (M3).
Acceptance: `card0` appears; `modetest -M exynos` lists CRTC/planes/connector; `modetest -s`
draws a test pattern and survives 10 flips; fb0 path untouched when KMS is off.
Estimate: 2–4 days.

**M2 — buffer/fence integration with panfrost7580**
dma-buf import into KMS (the vendor `decon_set_win_buffer` already consumes dma-buf/ion),
fences on atomic commit (`drm_atomic_helper` waits in-fences), GBM allocation from
panfrost exported to KMS, flips at vsync. Validate with `kmscube`, then `weston-simple-egl`.
Acceptance: 300 consecutive flips of a panfrost-rendered buffer with no underruns, no
`0x08` timeouts, correct colours (bit-identical to a CPU readback of the same buffer).
Estimate: 2–3 days (overlaps GPU work; the GPU path is already stable at 155 fps).

**M3 — coexistence and safety**
Make KMS-vs-fbdev a DT/boot choice, not a race: e.g. `status="disabled"` on the fb node in
an alternative DTS, or a single driver that registers both fb0 (legacy) and card0 (KMS) and
forwards fbs. Default image keeps nura-shell working; KMS enabled by a boot parameter.
Acceptance: both images boot; with KMS off nothing changes (X11 UI intact); with KMS on the
legacy fb is not registered and KWin gets master. Rollback is a boot-image swap.
Estimate: 1 day.

**M4 — Plasma Mobile session**
`lightdm` → `startplasmamobile` on `kwin_wayland`; zram for the 1.4 GB RAM; input via
evdev; brightness/rotation via the panel driver. Acceptance: home screen interactive,
app launch, no OOM in 30 min, suspend/resume smoke.
Estimate: 1–2 days after M3.

Total: ~2 weeks focused, with M0/M1 independent of the phone (build-host only) and M2+
needing boot cycles.

## 4. Risks

| Risk | Mitigation |
|---|---|
| Atomic backport API drift (3.10 `drm_crtc.c` predates the plane/fb split) | M0 keeps the legacy paths untouched; gate new code behind `DRIVER_ATOMIC`; compile-only first |
| Losing fb0 again (prior attempt) | never claim the DECON/DSIM compatibles; coexistence is an explicit milestone with rollback |
| KWin 6 also needs `DRM_CAP_*`/format modifiers not present in 3.10 | validate with `modetest`/`kmscube` at M1/M2 before touching Plasma |
| Memory pressure (Plasma 6 on 1.4 GB) | zram + `MALLOC_ARENA_MAX`, and the leak/race fixes already landed |
| Panel/DSI timing only proven by the fb driver | reuse the same timings and the vendored dsi low-level ops (`decon_display/decon_mipi_dsi_lowlevel.c`) |

## 5. Definition of done

Plasma Mobile 6.8 home screen runs at a usable frame rate on the J7, with `card0` (atomic)
provided by the DECON KMS subdriver, panfrost scanout through dma-buf, and a documented
rollback to the current X11/nura-shell image.

Plasma Mobile 6.8 home screen runs at a usable frame rate on the J7, with `card0` (atomic)

rollback to the current X11/nura-shell image.

content.name: task

arguments.context:
# Mission
Plasma Mobile 6.8 on the J7 requires a KMS device with **atomic modesetting**. The 3.10 DRM core has none, and the display is owned by the legacy fbdev `decon_fb`. Port plan and slice map: `/tmp/j7repo/docs/reports/decon-kms-plan.md` (read it first).

# Kernel tree (read-only; do not modify)
`/run/media/asdf/db69437b-ed35-414a-8bd1-bade16b06830/j7k/android_kernel_samsung_universal7580-2a746c1bc1a41eae05988c153f527c8a5dc72d07`
Key facts: pre-atomic DRM (`drm_plane_init` in `drivers/gpu/drm/drm_crtc.c:806`, no `drm_atomic.h`, no `DRIVER_ATOMIC`); vendor exynos DRM registers no subdriver (`exynos_drm_core.c:132-136` → `-EINVAL`); DECON fbdev driver `drivers/video/exynos/decon_7580/` already implements window programming (`decon_core.c:2185-2365`), dma-buf attach (`:1516-1737`), commit (`:2066-2183`), vsync (`decon-int_drv.c:73-124,542-615`), registers (`decon_reg_7580.c:414-668`); DT node `decon_fb@14830000` compatible `samsung,exynos5-decon_driver`, `status="disabled"` in SoC dtsi, enabled by the j7elte board dts; `dsim@14800000` compatible `samsung,exynos5-mipi-dsi`; `pd_disp` power domain.

# Repo & rules
`/tmp/j7repo` — commit only the files your slice owns; external disk for logs; no flash; no reboots; device access (if needed) always inside `flock /tmp/gpsdev.lock` and read-only. Phone: `user@172.16.42.1`, `SSH_ASKPASS=/tmp/ap.sh`, root via `/usr/local/bin/rootshell`, kernel int49. Do not edit other slices' files. Report file names are listed per task — do not create docs outside your own report.

tasks.name: KmsReq
tasks.solutionSpace: Requirements are not enumerated upstream for this tree; derive them from KWin 6.8 binaries/sources and DRM ioctl usage.
tasks.task:
# Target
Capability matrix: what KWin 6.8 / Plasma Mobile actually requires from the DRM driver.

# Change
Determine the exact DRM/KMS features kwin_wayland 6.8 needs: atomic commit, universal planes, ADDFB2 + IN_FORMATS/modifiers, PRIME import/export, DUMB buffers, vblank timestamps, cursor plane, async flip, dmabuf feedback, `DRM_CAP_*` values it queries, and which are fatal vs optional. Use the installed KWin on the phone (`strings`, `ldd`, config files, any source in `/usr`), libdrm/wayland headers on the device, plus upstream KWin 6.8 knowledge. For each requirement state: fatal?, testable with modetest/kmscube?, and the minimum driver support.

# Acceptance
`docs/reports/decon-kms-req.md` with a requirement→driver-support table, citations (file/version), and a "minimum viable atomic driver" checklist. Commit.

tasks.name: DeconApi
tasks.solutionSpace: How to expose the existing fb-shaped DECON API to DRM without owning the compatible is open; propose the minimal contract.
tasks.task:
# Target
Window-API contract for reusing `decon_set_win_config`/`decon_update_regs` from a DRM CRTC.

# Change
Extract the callable surface of `drivers/video/exynos/decon_7580/` that a KMS driver can reuse: mode set/enable/disable, window config + commit + shadow-protect/trigger, vblank wait/IRQ, dma-buf attach/format setup, suspend/resume and clock/power entry points. For each: signature, locking + context, PM requirements, and what is fb-specific (fb_info, framebuffer_alloc) vs genuinely reusable. Then write `code/gpu31/kms/decon_api.h` as the contract (function pointers or exported-symbol shim) plus `docs/reports/decon-kms-api.md` explaining the shim patch that would export these symbols (`EXPORT_SYMBOL`) and how the DRM subdriver is bound without claiming the fb compatible (e.g. Kconfig choice, platform data hand-off, or `device_find_child` on the fb device).

# Acceptance
Header + report with citations; the report must name the exact functions to export and the binding mechanism, with the failure modes of each option. Commit.

tasks.name: DsiPanel
tasks.solutionSpace: What the encoder must do is scattered across the vendor DSI/panel code; inventory open.
tasks.task:
# Target
DSI encoder/connector requirements for KMS.

# Change
Inventory the vendor MIPI-DSI + panel path (ea8061 on j7elte): DSI host init, lane/clock config, command writes, panel init/uninit sequence, video vs command mode, TE/vsync, backlight, reset GPIO and regulators, plus the timings currently used by the fb driver (porches, refresh). State what a DRM encoder/connector pair must call and in which order, and which parts can be reused directly (`decon_mipi_dsi_lowlevel.c`, dsi functions) vs need a DRM-native path. Include the suspend/resume ordering.

# Acceptance
`docs/reports/decon-kms-dsi.md` with an ordered call list, citations (file:line), and a short "encoder skeleton" pseudo-code. Commit.

tasks.name: DispPower
tasks.solutionSpace: Power/clock ordering evidence is spread across fb code, DT and PM files.
tasks.task:
# Target
Clocks, `pd_disp`, and runtime-PM contract for the display block.

# Change
Extract: the exact clock list the DECON/DSI drivers require and their rates (from `decon-int_drv.c` and DT), the `pd_disp` power-domain attach/use, regulator/backlight rails, suspend/resume hooks and what the fb driver does today (`decon_probe`, `decon_enable/disable`, `decon_remove`), plus the known rule that the bootloader leaves the display running (S-Boot DT payload note in `patches/drm-kms-coexist/DESIGN.md`). Define the sequencing the KMS driver must follow on probe, first modeset, runtime idle and system suspend, and what breaks if a clock/PD is missing (with the observed symptom).

# Acceptance
`docs/reports/decon-kms-power.md` with a state machine (mermaid) and citations. Commit.

tasks.name: KmsTooling
tasks.solutionSpace: Tooling availability on the arm64 pmOS device and against Mesa 20.3 is unverified.
tasks.task:
# Target
Test tooling for KMS: modetest/kmscube/libdrm and a repeatable flip/pattern test.

# Change
Determine what is already installed on the phone (`modetest`, `kmscube`, `weston-simple-egl`, libdrm version) and what must be built; produce build+run scripts under `code/gpu31/kms/tools/` that work with the existing Mesa at `/data/mesabuild/mesa20-b` (GBM + EGL surfaceless when no card0 yet) and against a future `card0`. Include a deterministic test-pattern + N-flip test with pass/fail criteria (pattern checksum, underrun/timeout counters from dmesg), and a 300-flip soak.

# Acceptance
`docs/reports/decon-kms-tooling.md` with the exact commands, what is missing today, and the scripts committed. Do not reboot the phone.

tasks.name: KmsCoexist
tasks.solutionSpace: KMS/fbdev coexistence is a design choice with rollback risk; options open.
tasks.task:
# Target
Coexistence and rollback: KMS on/off without losing `/dev/fb0` (the previous attempt lost it).

# Change
Compare options — (i) DT `status` switch via a second DTS + boot-image variants, (ii) a shared DECON core that registers both fb0 and card0, (iii) a boot parameter/`module_param` that makes the fb driver stand down before probe, (iv) Kconfig choice — on: driver-ownership clash risk, S-Boot DT payload rule, rollback cost, ability to A/B the same image, and what happens to Xorg/nura-shell in each. Produce the concrete DT/Kconfig/boot-param edits for the chosen option and a rollback runbook (the exact image to re-flash).

# Acceptance
`docs/reports/decon-kms-coexist.md` with a decision, the diff-level edits (file paths + lines), and the runbook. Commit.

tasks.name: PlasmaSession
tasks.solutionSpace: Session enablement details (service manager, autologin, env, input) depend on this image's Nura userland.
tasks.task:
# Target
Start Plasma Mobile as a wayland session on this image.

# Change
Inventory the current session stack (`xinit`/`nura-shell`, lightdm config, seat/input via evdev, DBus/elogind), then produce the config to autologin into `startplasmamobile` (kwin_wayland) once `card0` exists, with a toggle back to nura-shell. Cover: lightdm/sddm choice already installed, kwin env for GLES2 on panfrost (`KWIN_...`, `QT_QPA_PLATFORM`), input (`libinput` vs evdev), brightness/rotation hooks present in this image, and the first-boot checks. Deliver scripts/config in `code/gpu31/kms/session/` plus the runbook; do not enable it on the device yet.

# Acceptance
`docs/reports/decon-kms-session.md` with the exact files to install, a revert path, and a check list. Commit.

tasks.name: MemBudget
tasks.solutionSpace: Plasma 6 on 1.4 GB has no measured baseline; sizing is empirical.
tasks.task:
# Target
Memory budget for Plasma Mobile on 1.4 GB RAM.

# Change
Measure the current baseline (nura-shell/Xorg, fbwin) and estimate Plasma 6.8 needs (plasmashell, kwin_wayland, kwin's GL buffers, Qt pipelines) with citations for each component where possible. Then specify zram sizing/algorithm, swappiness, `MALLOC_ARENA_MAX`, and which Plasma services to disable on 1.4 GB. Provide a measurement script (`code/gpu31/kms/tools/memwatch.sh`) that samples MemAvailable/Shmem/zram and flags OOM, and acceptance thresholds for the session milestone.

# Acceptance
`docs/reports/decon-kms-memory.md` with baseline numbers measured on the phone, the config, and the thresholds. Device reads only, under the device lock; no reboots.

# Target
`exynos_drm7580_crtc.c` + the vendor export shim.

# Change
1) Write `patches/drm-kms/0100-decon-export-shim.patch`: make the needed vendor statics callable per `decon_api.h` (Layer B `decon_export_*` wrappers, EXPORT_SYMBOL_GPL, no behaviour change) and move `register_framebuffer()` to the probe tail with a guarded unregister in `decon_remove` (see `decon-kms-api.md` §6). 2) Implement `exynos7580_crtc_init`, `exynos7580_crtc_enable_link`, `exynos7580_crtc_disable_link` with atomic helpers: `atomic_check/begin/flush/commit`, mode_set via `decon_kms_*` (DsiPanel rule: the fallible DSI link enable lives in CRTC mode_set before `decon_reg_init`), full modeset after any pm_runtime cycle (DispPower), and the `mode_config_funcs.atomic_check/commit` ops. 3) Locking: no ww_mutex in this tree (M0 uses plain mutex + mode_config.mutex) — document why your order is deadlock-free.

# Acceptance
`docs/reports/decon-kms-crtc.md`; patches + source committed; build evidence (0 errors, your-file warnings listed); a host-side or target-side atomic TEST_ONLY path exercise if feasible without card0.

tasks.name: DeconPlane
tasks.solutionSpace: Plane/format mapping onto vendor windows is open: which fourcc map to which DECON formats, and how atomic update maps to decon_win_config.
tasks.task:
# Target
`exynos_drm7580_plane.c`.

# Change
Implement `exynos7580_planes_init`, `exynos7580_plane_atomic_update`, `exynos7580_plane_atomic_disable`: primary plane for CRTC 0 plus up to 2 overlays (MAX_WIN 3), fourcc→DECON format table (ARGB8888/XRGB8888/RGB565, plus NV12 if the vendor window supports it — verify in `decon_reg_7580.c`), src/dst rect validation (no scaling unless supported), zpos/alpha, and the window-shortage fallback (-ENOSPC). # Acceptance
`docs/reports/decon-kms-plane.md` with the format/limits table and evidence from the vendor code; patches + source committed; build evidence.

tasks.task:

`exynos_drm7580_dsi.c`.

# Acceptance
`docs/reports/decon-kms-dsi-encoder.md`; patches + source; build evidence; the exact dmesg lines M1 should produce at bind.

tasks.name: KmsDmabuf
tasks.solutionSpace: GEM/dma-buf import into a pre-shmem-split 3.10 DRM is open; the vendor iovmm mapping primitive is the constraint.
tasks.task:
# Target
`exynos_drm7580_dmabuf.c`.

# Change
Implement `exynos7580_gem_prime_import` and `exynos7580_fb_create`: dma-buf attach → GEM object (use the M0-era GEM helpers/drm_gem_prime_import with the driver's gem_free_object), IOVA mapping through the vendor `iovmm_map` primitive (NOT ion: `ion_iovmm_map` BUG_ONs on foreign exporters — see `decon-kms-api.md`), pitch/format checks and the fb object (no modifiers unless the driver advertises them). # Acceptance
`docs/reports/decon-kms-dmabuf.md` with the object lifecycle and ref counts; patches + source; build evidence; a host-side unit test of the format/pitch validation if practical.

tasks.name: KmsFence
tasks.solutionSpace: Vblank→fence completion on a pre-fence 3.10 tree (no struct fence/dma-resv) is open; coordinate with M0's vblank API adaptation.
tasks.task:

`exynos_drm7580_fence.c`.

# Acceptance
`docs/reports/decon-kms-fence.md` with a state/sequence diagram (mermaid) and the exact completion guarantees; patches + source; build evidence.

tasks.task:

[15d98088216bad45] KmsFbdev: KmsFbdev status + two integration facts (no action needed unless you disagree):

1) Contract gap found: `exynos_drm7580.h` has no way to turn a `struct drm_framebuffer *` into a scanout DMA address. KmsDmabuf owns fb creation, DeconPlane must scan it out, and fbdev needs an fb too. fb0 therefore uses the core `drm_fb_cma` framebuffer (drm_fbdev_cma_init on a drm_gem_cma_create() object) exactly as decon-kms-coexist.md §2.4 requires, and DeconPlane needs a `drm_fb_cma_get_gem_obj(state->fb, 0)->paddr` branch. I have messaged DeconPlane and KmsDmabuf; if you want instead a `exynos7580_fb_get_scanout()` in the contract header, that is your call — I am not editing the header.

2) 3.10 helpers crash on an atomic CRTC: `drm_fbdev_cma_init()` calls `drm_helper_disable_unused_functions()`, which dereferences `crtc->helper_private->disable`/`dpms` and `encoder->helper_private->disable`/`dpms` unguarded. Atomic CRTCs/encoders leave the legacy callbacks NULL, so fb0 init would NULL-deref. My series therefore carries a 2-hunk core fix (`drm_crtc_helper.c`: atomic-aware unused-function teardown) plus `drm_fb_helper.c`: `fix.id = "drmfb"` (absent in 3.10, needed so /sys/class/graphics/fb0/name is the standard value). Both are in my patch dir `patches/drm-kms/`; fold them into the M0/core series if you prefer.

[15d985e4c9abad6c] DeconCrtc: DeconCrtc: integration hazard in `0200` / `exynos_drm7580_main.c` (fix is 10 lines).

`main.c` defines a `static exynos7580_atomic_commit()` and installs it in `mode_config_funcs`. My crtc patch exports `exynos7580_atomic_commit()` + `exynos7580_atomic_check()` for exactly that table (the only two symbols beyond the header; documented in `docs/reports/decon-kms-crtc.md` §7.1). Static vs global does not collide at link time, so the driver silently uses main.c's copy — and that copy has two defects against the contract we agreed with KmsFence:

1. `if (async) return -EBUSY;` — KWin's flips are `NONBLOCK|PAGE_FLIP_EVENT`. Both `drm_mode_atomic_ioctl()` (NONBLOCK) and `drm_atomic_helper_page_flip()` go through `drm_atomic_async_commit()` → `config->funcs->atomic_commit(..., async = true)` → **-EBUSY**. Every non-blocking commit would fail; M1 needs the same tail for async.
2. It enables the link unconditionally, including commits that disable the CRTC (an extra DECON enable/disable cycle on every modeset-off).

Proposed fix (delete the static function, keep your table, declare the two):

```c
int exynos7580_atomic_check(struct drm_device *drm, struct drm_atomic_state *state);
int exynos7580_atomic_commit(struct drm_device *drm, struct drm_atomic_state *state,
			     bool async);

static const struct drm_mode_config_funcs exynos7580_mode_config_funcs = {
	.fb_create	= exynos7580_fb_create,
	.atomic_check	= exynos7580_atomic_check,
	.atomic_commit	= exynos7580_atomic_commit,
};
```

Mine is the same 4 steps you documented (link enable before `prepare_planes`, then prepare, swap, `exynos7580_commit_tail`), plus: async runs the same tail; the link is enabled only for crtc states that become active / have `mode_changed`; `-ENODEV` guard; `exynos7580_atomic_check()` is exactly `drm_atomic_helper_check()` so your table keeps the helper semantics. If you prefer to keep the function in main.c instead, at minimum drop the `async` -EBUSY and gate the link enable on `state->crtc_states[i]->active && (mode_changed || !crtc->state->active)` — but then the contract order exists in two files.

No action needed on `decon_kms_get()` / init order: your probe already calls `decon_kms_get(dev)` at :480, `exynos7580_planes_init()` at :310 before `exynos7580_crtc_init()` at :316, sets `drm->dev_private`, `drm_vblank_init` and `drm_mode_config_reset` — all as my slice expects.

arguments.content:
Integration hazard found by DeconCrtc — fix in your `0200` before assembly:

Your `exynos_drm7580_main.c` defines a `static exynos7580_atomic_commit()` with `if (async) return -EBUSY;`. KWin's flips are `NONBLOCK|PAGE_FLIP_EVENT`, which reach `atomic_commit(..., async=true)` — so every non-blocking commit would fail. DeconCrtc's crtc patch exports the agreed implementation.

Do exactly this: delete your static function and its `.atomic_commit` entry body, declare
```c
int exynos7580_atomic_check(struct drm_device *drm, struct drm_atomic_state *state);
int exynos7580_atomic_commit(struct drm_device *drm, struct drm_atomic_state *state,
			     bool async);
```
and install
```c
static const struct drm_mode_config_funcs exynos7580_mode_config_funcs = {
	.fb_create	= exynos7580_fb_create,
	.atomic_check	= exynos7580_atomic_check,
	.atomic_commit	= exynos7580_atomic_commit,
};
```
Its semantics: async runs the same tail (never -EBUSY); link enable only for crtc states that become active or have `mode_changed`; `-ENODEV` guard; `atomic_check` is `drm_atomic_helper_check()`. Rebuild with the crtc slice present (or its symbols declared) and push the corrected patch.

Working tree is clean, all content preserved, nothing lost or reverted; only attribution/commit shape of that one commit is off. Sorry — no further history edits made.

Four integration points from this slice:

1) REQUIRED CORE PATCH: patches/drm-kms/0005-core-drm-gem-cma-import-free.patch. main.c uses .gem_free_object = drm_gem_cma_free_object; 3.10's helper unconditionally dma_free_attrs()s, so freeing an imported object would release physical page 0 and leak the attachment. The patch makes it call drm_prime_gem_destroy(obj, obj->driver_private) when import_attach is set. Without it, the first KWin import that outlives a handle close corrupts memory. git apply --check clean on pristine+M0 and on top of KmsFbdev's 0003.

2) Kconfig: config DRM_EXYNOS7580 should `depends on EXYNOS_IOVMM_V6` (or EXYNOS_IOVMM). include/linux/exynos_iovmm.h does not declare iovmm_map() otherwise; my file has a hard #error as a backstop. Stock j7 config has EXYNOS_IOVMM_V6=y.

3) Bug outside my slice, in exynos_drm7580_main.c exynos7580_gem_prime_get_sg_table(): it fills sg_dma_address()/sg_dma_len() but never sg_set_page()/sg_set_buf(), so sg_page(sg) is NULL. The export path (drm_gem_map_dma_buf -> dma_map_sg) dereferences it when panfrost imports a KWin CREATE_DUMB buffer (req 21). Fix: sg_set_buf(sgt->sgl, cma_obj->vaddr, obj->size) before setting the DMA fields.

4) My patch adds only drivers/gpu/drm/exynos7580/exynos_drm7580_dmabuf.c; 0200 already lists exynos_drm7580_dmabuf.o, no Makefile hunk needed. exynos7580_fb_scanout(fb, plane, &addr) covers imported fbs, CMA dumb fbs and the drm_fb_cma fb0; plane 0 only; addfb2 rejects NV12 and any non-zero flags/modifiers.

Build: full drivers/gpu/drm/ with all current sibling sources, M0, core patches and this slice -> exit 0, no diagnostics in my file. Host validation test passes.

3. If neither works, we abandon modules and go back to built-in, but then we need a way to read the panic: check whether `EXYNOS_SNAPSHOT_PANIC_REBOOT=y` is what forces the reboot loop (disable it so a panic hangs instead, and see if pstore has the log), and make `ramoops` actually register (verify `ess_pstore_init` finds the bootloader `log_pstore` items on this boot image — on int49 `/sys/fs/pstore` is empty, which suggests it does not).
