grim needs wlr-screencopy, which KWin doesn't expose. Get the composite another way: `qdbus6 org.kde.KWin` to see whether a `/Screenshot` object with `screenshotFullscreen` still exists; if not, check `which xdg-desktop-portal-kde spectacle`, and otherwise write a ~30-line Qt6DBus client (Qt6 dev headers exist from the plasma-mobile build) that calls `/org/kde/KWin/ScreenShot2` `CaptureWorkspace` with a pipe fd and writes the PNG — that's the only way to see exactly what KWin composites, and it decides the panel question definitively.

The red-wallpaper test changed the screen, so plasmashell's desktop surface *is* being composited — that narrows what's left to the panel path alone (camera clipping makes the exact colour unreadable; don't chase it). Query the panel directly: `qdbus6 org.kde.plasmashell /PlasmaShell org.kde.PlasmaShell.evaluateScript 'print(JSON.stringify(panels().map(p=>({g:p.geometry,h:p.height,v:p.visibility}))))'` — geometry at y=0 h=200 with visibility 0 means the panel is mapped and KWin is dropping it (compositor side); anything else is shell side.

KWin is presenting flips again, so get its own view of the frame: `qdbus6 org.kde.KWin /Screenshot org.kde.KWin.Screenshot.screenshotFullscreen` (returns a saved path; if that API is absent try /org/kde/KWin/ScreenShot2) then pull the PNG over ssh. That immediately tells you whether the composite contains the panels/desktop (and the R↔G swap) or only a blank background — the one datum still missing after all the webcam photos.

Refinement on the leaked lock: this tree's `drm_mode_page_flip_ioctl` never calls `drm_modeset_lock_crtc()`, so `crtc->acquire_ctx` is NULL and `drm_modeset_legacy_acquire_ctx()` WARNs and hands you a ctx nothing owns — hence flip #1 locks and never releases. Patch `exynos7580_crtc_page_flip` to wrap the body in `drm_modeset_lock_crtc(crtc, plane)` (which stashes `crtc->acquire_ctx`) then `drm_modeset_unlock_crtc(crtc)` after the commit; that releases every lock taken through the hidden ctx. Note KWin itself uses the atomic ioctl (which does lock_all/unlock_all), so if its pageflip timeouts persist after this, the vblank arming is the next suspect.

That stack is the root cause: `exynos7580_crtc_page_flip` builds its state with `acquire_ctx == NULL`, so `drm_atomic_get_crtc_state()` takes `crtc->mutex` permanently; nothing ever releases it (the atomic-commit path you replaced is what normally drops the ioctl's locks), so flip #2 blocks in `drm_modeset_lock`. Fix as the core helper does: `drm_modeset_acquire_init(&ctx, 0)`, `state->acquire_ctx = &ctx`, then after `drm_atomic_async_commit()` call `drm_modeset_drop_locks(&ctx); drm_modeset_acquire_fini(&ctx);` — that should end the recurring "Pageflip timed out"/frozen-session cycle.

Legacy pageflip works (PAGE_FLIP seq=87), but KWin uses *atomic* commits — so extend fliptest to `drmModeAtomicCommit(crtc, req, DRM_MODE_ATOMIC_NONBLOCK | DRM_MODE_PAGE_FLIP_EVENT, NULL)` (props FB_ID/CRTC_ID, then MODE_ID) and poll for the event. If that times out while legacy flips work, the lost completion is in your atomic/async commit path (`crtc_state->event` handling), which is exactly what KWin hits.

KWin is alive but stuck on pageflip timeouts, and your commit tail is documented as synchronous — so stop depending on the flaky vblank IRQ: patch `exynos7580_complete_crtc_event()` to always call `exynos7580_send_event_now()` instead of arming for the next vblank (drop the `drm_vblank_get`/arm branch). That guarantees every commit's flip event reaches KWin and should end the recurring black screen; you can re-enable vblank arming later once the FRAME IRQ is proven reliable.

KWin keeps dying right after clients appear and you have no crash data — check `which strace gdb eu-stack`; if strace exists, start the session's kwin as `strace -f -tt -o /data/kwin.strace kwin_wayland ...` and add `ulimit -c unlimited` to cs21. The tail of the strace (last ioctl/syscall before SIGSEGV) will name the exact code path killing the compositor instead of more photo guessing.

Before more speculation about layers: /data persists across boots, so `/data/plasma-run/wayland-0` can be a stale socket from a previous session — check `ls -l /data/plasma-run/wayland-*` and grep clean-kwin.log for the socket name KWin actually bound. If KWin fell back to wayland-1 while cs21 waits for/exports wayland-0, you get exactly this "compositor alive, background only, nothing else composited" state.

Decisive, cheap test you haven't run: with the session up, `pkill -9 plasmashell`, run any client briefly to force a repaint, kill it, and photograph. If the same uniform blue is still there with no plasmashell at all, the blue is KWin's own scene background and plasmashell is drawing nothing (no wallpaper, no panels) — i.e., the remaining bug is entirely in plasmashell; if it goes black, the blue was plasmashell's desktop surface and only panels fail.

Panels end up `Windowed` (not hidden), so get their real geometry instead of guessing: `qdbus6 org.kde.plasmashell /PlasmaShell org.kde.PlasmaShell.evaluateScript 'print(JSON.stringify(panels().map(p => ({g: p.geometry, h: p.height, v: p.visibility}))))'`. If a 720×200 panel sits at y=0 and still isn't on the photo, the compositor is dropping it; that immediately splits KWin-side vs shell-side for good.

`QWindow::Hidden` means the panels are hidden by shell logic (Plasma Mobile auto-hides them on the home screen), not occluded — so the blue screen may simply be the mobileshell home screen, which is closer to done than the driver debug suggests. Interactive verification is only possible on the device: have the user swipe up from the bottom / tap, and confirm the app drawer or panel responds — that is the actual "usable GUI" criterion.

Panels *do* exist (`PanelView ... Windowed`), so the blocker is stacking: the desktop surface is covering them and your clients. Trace plasmashell (`WAYLAND_DEBUG=1 plasmashell 2>/data/ps.wd`) and compare `zwlr_layer_surface_v1.set_layer` values plus the surface sizes — the fullscreen home surface should be layer 0 (background); if it's 2 (top) it will sit above both the panels and every normal window, which matches every observation so far.

A fresh, untouched boot still shows a bare wallpaper with no UI, so this is the shell UI not loading, not KWin hiding it. Cheap decisive test: list `/usr/share/plasma/shells/` and rerun cs21 with `PLASMA_DEFAULT_SHELL=org.kde.plasma.desktop` — the desktop shell's panel is a normal dock window and would give a usable GUI independent of the mobileshell QML, and the log lines will show which shell actually loaded.

Widespread user-space faults across unrelated processes (pgrep, lslocks, sshd, elogind, kwin) after the display goes active smells like DMA corrupting RAM, not KWin: check `dmesg | grep -iE 'iommu|smmu|translation fault|external abort|SError|IOMMU'` and verify the DECON/GPU IOVA mappings (our iovmm scanout path) — a wrong IOVA/identity map would both corrupt memory and read wrong pixels.

Note the Comm values: elogind, gnome-keyring-d, rootshell, kwin — many unrelated processes are faulting, and dmesg is tainted `D` (oops occurred), so this is systemic memory corruption, not a KWin bug. Get the first fault's header + kernel stack: `dmesg | grep -n -m1 -B25 -A40 'Unhandled fault\|Internal error\|Unable to handle\|Call trace'` and check whether the faulting PC/LR are kernel addresses in your driver (iovmm/scanout mapping) — that's the thing to fix.

Session is fully dead again (kwin, plasmashell, qml6 all gone), so the recurring event to chase is that crash, not the colours: `dmesg | grep -E 'Comm:|fatal signal|Unhandled fault|Alignment trap|SIGBUS|SIGSEGV'` and the last ~60 lines of /data/clean-kwin.log to see which process faulted and whether the same signature kills every fresh session.

Zero pageflip timeouts this session plus `MESA: error: panfrost_batch_submit failed: 7` right as the screen went dark says the failure is GPU-side rendering, not presentation. cs21.sh itself warns a suspended tiler causes exactly this — check `/sys/bus/platform/devices/11400000.mali/power/runtime_status|control` (and autosuspend delay) at the moment the screen is dark, and whether submits recover after forcing the rail on; correlate with whether that Mesa error appears in the earlier logs where the UI did render.

The white fullscreen client staying invisible while the desktop wallpaper shows points to stacking, not rendering: the mobileshell homescreen window is above everything. Grep the plasma-mobile QML (`/data/build/plasma-mobile-6.8.3` shell dir) for `LayerShell`/`layer:` and `WindowStaysOnTop`, and check which layer/window-type the homescreen and panels request; if the homescreen sits in Top/Overlay, that single value explains both invisible panels and hidden clients.

A solid-white fullscreen client reading as patch avg (53,66,74) means either the client never commits a buffer or the panel isn't lit — resolve that first: `cat /sys/class/backlight/*/brightness /sys/class/backlight/*/actual_brightness`, write max, and take the photo within ~2 s of starting the white client. With the white client running, also `cat /sys/kernel/debug/dri/0/state` (or dmesg) to confirm the DECON plane's fb actually changed.

`supportInformation` has no window list; get ground truth from KWin itself via scripting: `qdbus6 org.kde.KWin /Scripting org.kde.kwin.Scripting.loadScript /tmp/wl.js` with `wl.js` = `workspace.windowList().forEach(w => print(w.caption, w.resourceClass, w.layer, w.frameGeometry, w.visible, w.minimized))`, then `runScript`. That tells you whether the client/panel/layer surfaces are actually mapped, at what geometry/layer — instead of inferring from webcam colours.

The cycle frames settle it: the screen changes between captures, so clients render and KWin presents — stop chasing colour/format theories. What the fresh capture actually shows is a bare wallpaper with no UI at all, so the remaining gap is plasmashell's shell UI never appearing; read `/data/clean-pshell.log` from the top (QML/plugin load errors) and check `qdbus6 | grep -i mobileshell` before touching the compositor again.

At this framing you can't tell whether a panel is on screen (the top bar would be a few pixels). Get a close-up where the phone fills the frame before judging "usable GUI", and in parallel verify a panel actually exists client-side: `grep -c 'plugin=org.kde.panel' /data/plasma-run/config/plasma-org.kde.plasma.desktop-appletsrc` and `grep -i 'panel\|layershell' /data/clean-pshell.log`.

`/proc/PID/stack` may be empty here; use `echo w > /proc/sysrq-trigger` to dump every blocked task's kernel stack to dmesg. The fliptests in `drm_modeset_lock_all` are just victims — the sysrq-w dump will show which task holds the orphaned modeset lock and what it's waiting on in your commit path.

Don't kill the stuck fliptests yet — capture evidence first: `cat /proc/7050/stack`, `cat /proc/7050/wchan`, `cat /proc/7050/syscall`. One of them is parked inside your atomic-commit path while holding `mode_config.mutex` (which is why the next GETRESOURCES blocks); that stack names the wait that never completes — the actual bug.

That `irq/557-flip_co` thread plus load 2 is a strong lead: dump `/proc/1531/stack`, `wchan`, and `stat` state — if the threaded flip-completion IRQ is parked in the DECON commit/commit-worker path, no flip event can ever be delivered (explaining the pageflip timeouts, black screen, and KWin "hang"s). Kill both leftover fliptest PIDs (7050, 7410) first so they aren't holding DRM master/fds while you inspect.

Stop guessing where fliptest hangs: launch it with `&` on the device and read `/proc/$PID/syscall` + `/proc/$PID/wchan` (+ `/proc/$PID/stack` if available). That names the exact blocking point (SETCRTC ioctl vs poll vs read) and tells you whether the driver or the client side is stalling.

modetest's `-M` wants the DRM driver name, which is `"exynos"` (DRIVER_NAME, exynos_drm7580_main.c:56), not the module name — so `modetest -M exynos -D /dev/dri/card0` after stopping kwin. Also preload your `/home/user/addfb_shim.so` when you run it: system libdrm 2.4.134 sends the modifier-bearing fb_cmd2 ABI, so modetest will hit the same AddFB2 mismatch your shim exists to fix.

Before attributing the black screen to flips: check the panel backlight (`cat /sys/class/backlight/*/brightness`, set to max) and see whether "Pageflip timed out" also appeared in the earlier sessions' kwin logs where content was visibly rendering. If those timeouts are pre-existing noise, the current black screen is backlight/DSI power, not flip completion.

`exynos7580_complete_crtc_event` arms the flip event on the next vblank, and the only way it's ever sent is `exynos7580_vblank_irq` → `drm_handle_vblank()`. So check whether the DECON IRQ is actually firing: sample `/proc/interrupts` (decon) twice a second apart while a client animates. If the count is static, the frame-done/vblank IRQ is dead on this boot (DSI/crtc bring-up), which explains the pageflip timeouts and black screen — and neither the read fix nor min_width is involved.

Pageflip timeouts now point at the driver's KmsFence tail, not userspace: grep dmesg for the newest `exynos7580_atomic_commit`/`exynos7580_page_flip` lines and check each kwin thread's wchan (`for t in /proc/$K/task/*; do echo $t $(cat $t/wchan); done`). If the commit tail is parked in its next-vblank wait, the vblank IRQ isn't advancing and no read-path change will fix it — instrument the KmsFence arming/IRQ handler next.

Black screen with kwin and plasmashell both alive (K=4716) after a long idle smells like DPMS/blanking, which would also explain several earlier "frozen frame"/"nothing renders" captures. Before interpreting any black photo, force the output on via `qdbus6 org.kde.KWin /DPMS org.kde.kwin.DPMS.setMode 0` (or equivalent) and re-capture; keep a continuously animating client running during idle periods.

Root cause is upstream of fb_create, and it's a one-line driver bug: `exynos_drm7580_main.c:339-340` sets `mode_config.min_width/min_height = 64`, and core `drm_mode_addfb2` (drm_crtc.c:2496) rejects any fb smaller than that *before* calling fb_create — exactly why the 32x32 ARGB cursor AddFB2 returns EINVAL with no `exynos7580_fb_create` print. Set min_width/min_height to 1 and let `exy7580_fb_check`'s 128-byte stride rule enforce the real DECON limit at scanout instead of at fb creation.

dmesg has a kernel register dump around t=777s — that's an oops, not a clean -EINVAL; whatever task issued it was killed (likely your vanished kwin_wayland). Pull the full crash block (`dmesg | grep -n -B20 -A40 'Unable to handle\|Internal error\|BUG:\|Call trace'`) to get the faulting PC/LR and `Comm:` line — that, not the fb_check rules, is the actual root cause to fix.

Before rebuilding the driver: check the tail of /data/clean-kwin.log and dmesg to confirm *why* kwin_wayland exited (abort/assert/SIGSEGV vs. killed). The 32x32 ARGB fb is almost certainly KWin's cursor sprite — KWin normally logs "Failed to create framebuffer" for that and falls back to a software cursor rather than dying, so treating that EINVAL as the crash cause may be wrong.

Don't guess the 32x32 EINVAL: `exy7580_fb_check()` in exynos_drm7580_dmabuf.c returns -EINVAL from ~10 branches with no printk, while `exynos7580_fb_create` already pr_info's each call. Add a distinct pr_info/pr_err to each failing branch (especially the `need > size` check — a 32x32 ARGB linear buffer needs 4096 bytes and an AFBC/tiled panfrost dmabuf is smaller), rebuild, and reproduce; dmesg will name the exact condition.

Four identical cyan frames during a colour-cycle proves the visible surface isn't your cycle client. Before any more captures, `pkill -9 -x qml6` and confirm `pidof qml6` is empty (you already found stale 5653 earlier) — an opaque Top-layer probe left running from a previous test would sit above every new client and freeze the screen on its colour, which fits all the "nothing renders" observations.

Read that last capture as the probe, not the wallpaper: it's flat saturated magenta, whereas the wallpaper shot had the photo pattern. If `pidof plasmashell` was indeed empty, then layer Top *does* render with no desktop window — so the panels are being occluded by the mobile-shell desktop window, not un-presented. Proceed with the layer sweep rather than re-killing plasmashell.

Now restart plasmashell and sweep the probe across layers 0–4 with the desktop present: whichever layer shows magenta tells you the mobile-shell desktop's own layer. If Overlay shows above the desktop while Top doesn't, the desktop is a Top-layer surface and the panels are simply stacked under it — fix on the shell side (put the homescreen on Background/Bottom, or panels on Overlay) instead of KWin.

There's no KWin source tree on the device, so any KWin fix means a fresh clone + full rebuild — expensive. You already have `/data/.../plasma-mobile-6.8.3` built locally: grep its shell QML for `LayerShell`/`layerShell` first and, if the panel/statusbar surfaces are created there, patch the shell (incremental rebuild) instead of KWin.

Check the shell actually exists before patching anything: `pacman -Q plasma-mobile`, `ls /usr/share/plasma/shells/`, and grep /data/clean-pshell.log for shell-load errors. If `org.kde.plasma.mobileshell` isn't installed, plasmashell silently shows only a desktop view — which alone explains "wallpaper visible, no panels" without any KWin layer-shell bug.

Your layer probe is only a proxy — before patching KWin, trace plasmashell's own Wayland traffic (start it with `WAYLAND_DEBUG=1`, log to file) and grep for `get_layer_surface`/`zwlr_layer_surface_v1.configure`/`wl_surface.commit`. If plasmashell never creates a panel layer surface at all, the bug is client-side (panel config/shell loading) and KWin work would be wasted.

The wire trace only shows the client side; enable KWin's own debug categories (`KWIN_LOGS="kwin_layershell"` — plus `kwin_core`) when starting cs21 so KWin logs its mapping decision for the layer surface (no output? no buffer? wrong layer?). That will tell you whether to patch KWin or the client far faster than more WAYLAND_DEBUG runs.

That `panfrost_batch_submit failed: 7` on every frame explains the black screen — rendering isn't reaching the GPU, so it may be environmental (post-reboot Mesa/panfrost) rather than caused by int104. Isolate it: reload/reboot with int103 on this same image and check whether the panfrost submit error and black screen persist; don't keep debugging drm_read until you know which change introduced it.

Don't trust the webcam photo for this: grab KWin's composited output via its DBus screenshot API (org.kde.KWin.ScreenShot2 CaptureWorkspace) so you can tell "KWin isn't presenting/page-flipping" from "nothing is drawn". Also check the kwin log for a drmHandleEvent error under int104 — on this 3.10 kernel libdrm's read path never expected -EAGAIN, so your int104 change may be erroring out KWin's whole DRM event loop (which would explain all surfaces, xdg included, going black).

Layer surface now commits (`ATTACH=7`, `CONF=2`) yet is never presented while xdg toplevels render — so before forking KWin, take the cheap side first: patch plasma-workspace's PanelView to skip LayerShellQt (panels become ordinary windows + keep-above), which by your own evidence does render, and that alone should give a usable mobile shell; fixing KWin's layer-surface/output association can follow afterwards.

The stack now shows `exynos7580_read → drm_read` still blocking despite the forced O_NONBLOCK — this kernel's `drm_read` waits before it honours the flag, so the wrapper can't fix it that way. Instead check inside the wrapper first: `if (list_empty(&file_priv->event_list)) return -EAGAIN;` (drm_file is available via drmP.h) and only then call `drm_read` to consume the pending event — that keeps KWin's main loop from ever sleeping in read without hard-coding a 1 s stall.

Before forking KWin, grep the post-int103 wire log for the layer surface's own lifecycle: `zwlr_layer_surface_v1` `.configure(...)` from KWin, then `wl_surface.attach` + `commit` from the client. Your `CONF=2` count may be xdg_surface configures; if the layer probe never gets a layer configure or never attaches a buffer, "KWin doesn't present layer surfaces" is unproven and a KWin fork would be hours wasted.

TRIGCON=00000040` and `exynos7580_plane_commit_frame: vsync retry rc=-110` — DECON never latches a new frame, so the panel keeps the frame from the first commit (explaining cyan/red never matching the composite). In PanelView's enum, 3 is *WindowsGoBelow* — with the 720×1280 desktop window covering the screen the panel is placed below it and Qt hides it (`exposureChanged(Hidden)`), exactly what the log shows. old='''	/*
	 * Take the interrupt reference first, then arm.  The order matters:
	 * the arm must never be visible without a reference, because

	 */
	if (!exynos7580_vblank_available(drm, pipe) ||
	    drm_vblank_get(drm, pipe) != 0) {
		dev_dbg(drm->dev,
			"crtc %u: no vblank, completing flip event immediately\\n",
			pipe);
		exynos7580_send_event_now(drm, -1, e);
		return;
	}

	spin_lock_irqsave(&drm->event_lock, flags);
	exynos7580_arm_vblank_event(drm, pipe, e);
	spin_unlock_irqrestore(&drm->event_lock, flags);'''
new='''	/*
	 * int109: deliver immediately instead of arming for a vblank.
	 *
	 * The DECON frame interrupt is dead on this stack: /proc/interrupts
	 * shows line 234 (14830000.decon_fb) frozen while the DSI line
	 * advances at 60 Hz, so drm_handle_vblank() never runs and every
	 * armed flip event is lost.  KWin then reports "Pageflip timed out"
	 * and stops presenting even though the (synchronous) DECON commit

	 * The vendor commit ran decon_wait_for_vsync()/decon_update_regs()
	 * before this point, so the scanout buffer is programmed; completing
	 * the event here is what userspace needs to release its buffer.
	 */
	if (exynos7580_vblank_available(drm, pipe))
		exynos7580_send_event_now(drm, (int)pipe, e);
	else
		exynos7580_send_event_now(drm, -1, e);'''

open(p,"w").write(s)
print("patched")

The fix: replace `sg_set_buf(... vaddr ...)` with `sg_set_page(sgt->sgl, phys_to_page(cma_obj->paddr), obj->size, cma_obj->paddr & ~PAGE_MASK)`.

Note: `sg_set_buf` = sg_set_page(sg, virt_to_page(buf), buflen, offset_in_page(buf)). virt_to_page on vmalloc → bogus. For CMA, `cma_obj->vaddr` may be vmalloc (dma_alloc_coherent with large sizes uses vmalloc on ARM). `cma_obj->paddr` is the physical base.

The advisor's fix: sg_set_page(sg, phys_to_page(paddr), size, paddr & ~PAGE_MASK). Note phys_to_page takes a phys_addr_t; for highmem kernels this is fine (this is arm64, no highmem).

But careful: the sg entry length should be obj->size (page-aligned length is handled by dma_map_sg). Also keep sg_dma_address/len.

Also for imported objects (import_attach), cma_obj->paddr is a DECON IOVA as per import; the comment says imported buffers aren't re-exported. To be safe, guard: if obj->import_attach → return ERR_PTR(-EINVAL)? The comment claims unsupported. But the finding suggests panfrost (kmsro) imports card0 dumb buffers — i.e., our dumb buffers exported to panfrost. That's the export path with vaddr.

And panfrost importing our buffer passes through *panfrost's* import, which uses the sg table we provide (via dma_buf ops) and maps it into the GPU's address space. If our sg entry has a garbage page, panfrost maps garbage → AS0 TRANSLATION_FAULT. That fits perfectly with KWin's kmsro usage: KWin renders into dumb buffers? Actually KWin's scanout buffers are created via CREATE_DUMB then exported to panfrost for rendering (the comment says exactly this: requirement 21).

So this is very likely the root cause of the MMU faults. Fix it.

Also add `vmap` correctness: for CMA buffers, vaddr is fine for CPU mapping; panfrost may call vmap for the fd — returning vaddr is OK.

Implement the sg fix + a pr_info logging obj->import_attach/paddr (finding 4 evidence), build int111, deploy, test: check dmesg for panfrost MMU faults after KWin runs.

import struct, hashlib

The "tail" is actually a **DTB** (device tree blob) — wait, the strings show DT property names ("compatible", "regulator-name", etc.). But we already accounted for dt_size=313344 at offset 27017216. The tail at 27330560 shows DTB-like content...

Hmm: magic "\x00\x00.zKEY" — that looks like FDT? No, FDT magic is 0xd00dfeed.

Let me reconsider: maybe the header's dt_size=313344 is the *first* DTB, and there are MORE DTBs appended (Samsung boot images often have multiple DTBs / dtb appended for various board revisions).

The content at tail_off starts with 0x0000 + ".zKEY" — not an FDT header. So it might be a *second stage* or an extra DTB in a different format (Samsung's "dtb" appended by the bootloader with tags?).

import struct, sys, hashlib

def parse(d):
    magic = d[:8]
    assert magic == b'ANDROID!', magic
    vals = struct.unpack_from('<10I', d, 8)
    ks,kaddr,rs,raddr,ss,saddr,tags,page,dtsz,unused = vals
    def al(n): return (n + page - 1)//page*page
    ko = page
    ro = ko + al(ks)
    so = ro + al(rs)
    do = so + al(ss)
    to = do + al(dtsz)
    return dict(vals=vals, ks=ks, rs=rs, ss=ss, dtsz=dtsz, page=page,
                ko=ko, ro=ro, so=so, do=do, to=to, al=al)

def repack(src, new_kernel_bytes, out):
    d = open(src,'rb').read()
    p = parse(d)
    page = p['page']; al = p['al']
    hdr = bytearray(d[:page])
    ks, rs, ss, dtsz = len(new_kernel_bytes), p['rs'], p['ss'], p['dtsz']
    struct.pack_into('<I', hdr, 8, ks)
    ramdisk = d[p['ro']:p['ro']+p['rs']]
    second  = d[p['so']:p['so']+p['ss']]
    dt      = d[p['do']:p['do']+p['dtsz']]
    tail    = d[p['to']:]
    body = bytearray()
    body += new_kernel_bytes
    body += b'\0' * (al(ks) - ks)
    body += ramdisk + b'\0' * (al(rs) - rs)
    body += second  + b'\0' * (al(ss) - ss)
    body += dt      + b'\0' * (al(dtsz) - dtsz)
    body += tail
    img = bytes(hdr) + bytes(body)
    open(out,'wb').write(img)
    return img

if __name__ == '__main__':
    src, kpath, out = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2], sys.argv[3]
    kb = open(kpath,'rb').read() if kpath != '-' else None
    if kb is None:
        d = open(src,'rb').read(); p = parse(d); kb = d[p['ko']:p['ko']+p['ks']]
    img = repack(src, kb, out)
    print('wrote', out, len(img), 'bytes', 'md5', hashlib.md5(img).hexdigest())
